URDAY, AERLL CAD) -PRAVDA TODAY QUOTED FRENCH PREMIER 
EDGAR FAURE AS SAYING BIG FOUR TALKS COULD BE FRUITFUL IF~THE 
POWERS WOULD TAKE INTO ACCOUNT EACH OTHER'S “LEGITIMATE SECURITY 


REQUIREMENTS." 
THE FRENCH PREMIER'S STATEMENT WAS INCLUDED IN AN INTERVIEW 
GIVEN TO TWO PRAVDA CORRESPONDENTS IN PARIS.» 
THE CORRESPONDENTS SAID FAURE WAS ASKED FOR COMMENT ABOUT 
SOVIET PREMIER NIKOLAI BULGANIN'S STATEMENT OF MARCH 26 THAT HE TOOK 
A *POSITIVE ATTITUDE* TOWARD A BIG FOUR MEETING. THEY QUOTED HIM 


AS GIVING THIS REPLY: 
"THIS STATEMENT (OF BULGANIN'S) CONSTITUTES A VERY IMPORTANT 


POSITIVE FACT. I CONSIDER THAT THE LESSENING OF INTERNATIONAL TENSION 
DEPENDS MAINLY ON THE™COMMON EFFORTS OF ALL INTERESTED POWERS, © 
TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE LEGITIMATE SECURITY REQUIREMENTS OF EACH 

OF THESE POWERS. 

*I WISH THAT NEGOTIATIONS COULD DEVELOP IN THIS SPIRT. IF THIS 
CONDITION IS OBSERVED THEY CAN BE FRUITFULe THESE. NEGOTIATIONS 
WOULD BE RENDERED EASIER BY A RELAXING OF TENSION IN RELATIONS BETWEEN 
THE UeSeSeRe AND THE UeSeAe® 

THE PRAVDA REPORT COMMENTED THAT RATIFICATION OF THE PARIS 
AGREEMENTS FOR THE REARMAMENT OF WESTERN GERMANY CREATED A NEW 
SITUATION IN EUROPE WHICH WAS BOUND TO BE REFLECTED IN THE ECONOMIC 
AND CULTURAL RELATIONS OF FRANCE AND THE SOVIET UNION, 

IN THE INTERVIEW FAURE INSISTED THAT. FRANCE'S RATIFICATION OF THE 
PARIS AGREEMENTS WAS COMPATIBLE WITH THE FRENCH-SOVIET FRIENDSHIP 
TREATY OF 1944. HE STRESSED THAT HE WAS DETERMINED TO STRENGTHEN 
ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL RELATIONS BETWEEN THE TWO COUNTRIES, 

THE PRAVDA WRITER, YURI ZHUKOV SAID THIS “CANNOT BUT GIVE RISE TO 
CERTAIN COMMENTS.® 

“IT IS WELL KNOWN THAT DUE TO THE PARIS AGREEMENTS FRANCE 
BECOMES AN ALLY OF GERMAN MILITARISM,® HE DECLARED. 

HE SAID THAT ALTHOUGH THE SOVIET UNION PLACED GREAT IMPORTANCE 
ON ITS ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL RELATIONS WITH FRANCE THESE RELATIONS 
COULD NOT HELP BUT BE AFFECTED BY THE RATIFICATION. 

ZHUKOV'S COMMENT, HOWEVER, WAS MODERATE COMPARED WITH SOME THAT 
WERE VOICED HERE BEFORE FRANCE COMPLETED RATIFICATION.

LONDON, APRIL 2 (AP)-A MARKED STEP-DOWN IN THE PEIPING RADIO'S 
SABRE RA RAIS ON HERE TODAY THAT THE CHINESE REDS 
MAY BE TURNING AWAY FROM THEIR BOASTED PLANS TO CAPTURE FORMOSA. 

MONITORS OF RED CHINA'S DAILY PROPAGANDA BROADCASTS SAID THEY 
HAD NOTED THESE TWO TRENDS: 

1. A TAPERING OFF IN THE PAST 10 DAYS OF THE ONCE FREQUENT 
REFERENCES TO CHINESE COMMUNIST ARMIES AND THEIR MISSION TO "LIBERATE 
TAIWAN (FORMOSA) .® 

2. SOME SIGNS THAT THE REDS ALSO WERE WATERING DOWN THEIR 
VITRIOLIC ABUSE OF THE CHINESE NATIONALIST LEADER, CHIANG KAI-SHEK. 

DIPLOMATIC SOURCES SPECULATED THAT BRITAIN AND RUSSIA MAY BE 
REGISTERING SOME SUCCESS IN BACKSTAGE EFFORTS TO PERSUADE RED 
CHINA'S PREMIER CHOU EN-LAI TO EXERCISE RESTRAINT IN THE PRESENT 
TENSE SITUATION. | 

THE MONITORS SAID THERE HAD BEEN NO SINGLE REFERENCE TO THE 
*LIBERATION® OF FORMOSA IN PEIPING BROADCASTS IN THE LAST THREE DAYS. 

THE PEIPING RADIO TODAY SAID THAT “ARMED OCCUPATION" OF THE 
ISLAND WAS THE CAUSE OF FAR EAST TENSION, BUT IT MADE NO MENTION OF 
DETERMINATION TO TAKE THE ISLAND. THIS WAS THE RADIO'S FIRST 
MENTION OF FORMOSA IN SEVERAL DAYS. THE BROADCAST CHARGED THAT THE 
WESTERN PRESS WAS “DISTORTING" THE SITUATION AND "SLANDERING THE 
POSITION TAKEN BY CHINA AND THE SOVIET UNION." 

IN THE SAME TIME THE MONITORS NOTED THE RED RADIO HAD CARRIED 
ONLY ONE REFERENCE TO THE “CHIANG KAI-SHEK GANG" THOUGH UP TO A FEW 
DAYS AGO VIRTUALLY EVERY PEIPING BROADCAST FEATURED THE "EVIL WAR 
PREPARATIONS OF THE TRAITOROUS CHIANG KAI=-SHEK CLIQUE.” 

DIPLOMATS SAID IT MAY BE POSSIBLE THAT THE PROPAGANDA BACKTRACKING 
REFLECTS DIPLOMATIC ACTIVITY AIMED AT TALKS ON A FORMOSA SETTLEMENT, 
BRITAIN HAS SOUGHT TO ENLIST THE AID OF THE SOVIET UNION SINCE 
JANUARY IN AN ATTEMPT TO QUIET THE EXPLOSIVE SITUATION IN FORMOSA 
STRAITs BOTH HAVE EXPRESSED FEARS THAT A MAJOR CLASH IN THE AREA 

MIGHT START ANOTHER WORLD WAR» 

THE SOVIET UNION ON FEBe 12 PROPOSED A 10-POWER CONFERENCE ON 
FORMOSA. THE 10 POWERS SUGGESTED BY RUSSIA INCLUDE THE UNITED 
STATES BUT NOT THE CHINESE NATIONALISTS. THE BRITISH REPLIED THAT 
NO CONFERENCE COULD SUCCEED WITHOUT BOTH SIDES TO THE DISPUTE 
SITTING INe 

BRITISH FOREIGN SECRETARY SIR ANTHONY EDEN PUT THIS VIEW BEFORE THE 
HOUSE OF COMMONS ON FEB. 14, AND ADDED, “THESE EXCHANGES ARE NOT 
VET CLOSED AND WHEN I AM IN A POSITION TO DO SO I WILL MAKE ANOTHER 
REPORT TO THE HOUSE."

—TAIPEL, GORMOSA, APRIL 2.-(AP)-~ THERE IS A NEW KIND OF TENSION THESE 
DAYS IN FORMOSA. NOT A WAR TENSION, A SURRENDER TENSION. FORMOSA IS 
TENSE WITH DREAD THAT THE UNITED STATES IS IN THE PROCESS OF DECIDING 
--IF SHE HASN'T ALREADY DECIDED--TO WRITE OFF MATSU AND QUEMOY. 

WHAT IS THE EVIDENCE? 

AMERICAN REPRESENTATIVES HERE ARE MAKING A DAILY SOUNDING OF 
FORMOSA MORALE AND REPORTING TO WASHINGTON. THEY REPORT ON MONEY 
EXCHANGE RATES, PRICES AND OTHER THINGS THAT REFLECT FEAR OR 
DISCOURAGEMENT OR HOPE, 

*THEY WOULDN'T BE DOING THIS IF THEY WERE GOING TO HELP US FIGHT 
FOR MATSU AND QUEMOY" SAID ONE NATIONALIST. OFFICER. “THEY WOULDN'T 
HAVE TO WORRY ABOUT MOR MORALE THEN.® 

SOME CHINESE EVEN PROFESS TO SEE IN THE IMMINENT DEPARTURE ON 
HOME LEAVE OF AMBASSADOR KARL RANKIN A GLOOMY OMEN. RANKIN, FIVE YEARS 
ON FORMOSA AND DEEPLY SYMPATHETIC WITH THE NATIONALIST CAUSE, IS, 
THEY SAY, BEING SPARED THE PAINFUL TASK OF BREAKING THE BAD NEWS. 

EVERYBODY AGREES THAT THE EFFECT HERE OF ANOTHER BLOODLESS 
SURRENDER LIKE TACHENS AND NANCHISHAN WOULD BE BAD. ONE HIGHLY- 
PLACED AMERICAN SAID *IT MIGHT EVEN BE FATAL.® 

SOME EVEN DOUBT THAT CHIANG KAI-SHEK'S LEADERSHIP COULD SURVIVE IT. 
SOME SAY THE ARMY MIGHT REBEL. THESE SOLDIERS, WHO HAVE PUT THEIR 
PERSONAL LIVES IN ADJOURNMENT EVEN TO ESCHEWING MARRIAGE AS THEIR 
PART TOWARD COUNTER=INVASION, MIGHT BLOW THEIR TOPS IF THEY GET THE 
NOTION THAT THE PURPOSE OF ALL THIS SELF DENIAL AND PATIENT 
PREPARATION HAD DISAPPEARED. 

MORE SURRENDERS WOULD HAVE A SLOWER BUT POSSIBLY EVEN WORSE 
EFFECT ON NON-COMMUNIST SOUTHEAST ASIA, SOME NATIONALIST QUARTERS 
ARGUE. THESE PEOPLE SAY THAT THE COLD WAR HAS REACHED A POINT IN ASIA 
WHERE A REVERSAL IN ONE AREA AFFECTS ALL OTHER AREAS. 

} - HE SAME GROUP ALSO SAYS THAT ANO 
SURRENDER TO THE COMMUNISTS, SPECIALLY A NON-FIGHTING SURRENDER, 
MIGHT START AN IRREPRESSIBLE CAMPAIGN OF SUBVERSION IN FORMOSA 
REJUVINATE THE HUKS IN LUZON, REKINDLE THE TERRORISTS IN MALAYA AND

SAN FRANCISCO, APRIL 4 (AP)-SCIENTISTS ARE FORCED TO DEAL WITH THE 
REMOTE POSSIBILITY THAT ATOMIC REACTORS WILL BLOW UP AND SPREAD THEIR 
RADIOACTIVE POISONS OVER THE COUNTRY, DRe EDWARD he NOTED 
FIGURE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE HYDROGEN BOMB, SAID TODAY. 

THE CHANCES ARE REMOTE BECAUSE OF ELABORATE SAFEGUARDS. BUT THE 
POSSIBILITY HAS TO BE CONSIDERED BECAUSE ACCIDENTS CAN HAPPEN IN SPITE 
a DRe TELLER TOLD A WESTERN CONFERENCE ON ATOMIC 
EN . 

A REACTOR EXPLOSION WOULD NOT BE LIKE THE BLAST OF AN ATOMIC BOMB 
HE ADDED. IT WOULD BE A FLAREUP THAT MIGHT DISINTEGRATE THE STRUCTURE 
AND SCATTER ITS TONS OF "HOT" MATERIAL INTO THE AIR AS FINE PARTICLES, 

ay eae THEREAFTER WOULD BE THE FALLOUT OF THIS MATERIAL OVER A 
WID 2 

DRe TELLER SPOKE AS A MEMBER OF AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE OF THE ATOMIC 
ENERGY COMMISSION. THIS COMMITTEE PASSES UPON THE SAFETY CHARACTER- 
ISTICS OF REACTOR DESIGN AND OPERATION. 

DRe TELLER DISCLOSED THAT THE FIRST DEATH FROM AN ATOMIC EXPLOSION 
OCCURRED AT LOS ALAMOS SHORTLY AFTER A CIRCULAR WAS DISTRIBUTED To 
THE PERSONNEL SAYING THE LABORATORY HAD COMPLETED ITS BIG JOB 
SUCCESSFULLY WITHOUT A FATALITY. 

ALL PERSONNEL IN THE A-BOMB LABORATORY WERE WELL TRAINED AND AWARE 


OF THE DANGERS AND EVERY SAFETY PRECAUTION WAS TAKEN. 
BUT ONE OF THE YOUNG SCIENTISTS, DRe HARRY Ke DAGLIAN, VIOLATED A 
SAFETY RULE BY GOING TO WORK ALONE ON FISSIONABLE MATERIAL, DReTELLER 
SAID. HIS HAND SLIPPED. THERE WAS A FLAREUP LIKE THE SPUTTER OF AN 
ARC WELDER AND HE WAS SUBJECTED TO ENORMOUS HEAT AND RADIATION. HE 
DIE ° 
AFTER ANOTHER LOS ALAMOS SCIENTIST, DRe LOUIS SLOTIN, MET DEATH 
UNDER SIMILAR CIRCUMSTANCES. RULES WERE VIOLATED SOMEWHERE, AND 
SOMETHING SLIPPED WHILE SLOTIN WAS AT WORK.

TOKYO, APRIL 5 (AP)-CHINA'S COMMUNIST MASTERS CRACKED DOWN WITH 
HARSH NEW DISCIPLINE IN PARTY RANKS IN THE WAKE OF THEIR FIRST PURGE 
OF TOP MEN SINCE THEY WON CONTROL OF 600 MILLION CHINESE IN 1949.

IT SAID THE COMMUNIST PARTY HAD PURGED KAO KANG, THE “MANCHURIAN 
STALIN® WHO BOSSED RED CHINA'S FALTERING FIVE-YEAR PLAN, AND JAO SHU- 
SHIH, A SHANGHAI STALWART WHO RULED SIX BIG EASTERN PROWINCES IN THE 
FARLY DAYS OF THE RED REGIME. 

KAO COMMITTED SUICIDE, PEIPING SAID. JAO, FORMER PARTY SECRETARY 
FOR EAST CHINA, "HAS NEVER SHOWN ANY SIGNS OF REPENTENCE AND NOW

PARTY AND THE STATE® WITH RED ARMY HELP.

PARIS) APRIL 5 C(AP)-PREMIER EDGAR FAURE SAID TODAY FRANCE MAY SOON 
TAKE THE LEAD IN PROPOSING A JOINT EUROPEAN DEVELOPMENT OF NUCLEAR 
ENERGY FOR PEACEFUL AND INDUSTRIAL PURPOSES. 

SPEAKING TO A LUNCHEON MEETING OF THE FOREIGN PRESS ASSNe THE PREMIER 
SAID THE INTERNATIONAL APPROACH IS THE BEST WAY TO PROMOTE ATOMIC ENERGY 
IN EUROPE BECAUSE, GENEALLY SPEAKING, NO SINGLE NATION OF EUROPE 
HAS THE MEANS ; 

FAURE WAS QUESTIONED ABOUT HIS STATEMENT IN A RECENT NEWS 
CONFERENCE WHICH HAD BEEN INTERPRETED TO MEAN FRANCE MUST SOON MAKE A 
HYDROGEN BOMB TO MAINTAIN HER RANK AS A MAJOR WORLD POWER. HE SAID 
THAT IMPRESSION NEEDED TO BE CORRECTED. 

"WE ARE NOT NOW OBLIGED TO MAKE A BOMB TO MAINTAIN OUR PLACE, 

AND I HOPE THIS CAN BE AVOIDED," FAURE SAID. "FRANCE HAS A LAG TO 
OVERCOME. SHE CAN WORK OUT A TWO-YEAR PROGRAM._WHICH WOULD NOT NECESSAR- 
ILY BE OF A MILITARY NATURE, BUT WHICH WOULD RATHER BE AIMED AT INDUS- 
TRIAL APPLICATIONS OF THIS ENERGY. 

"IT IS ONLY AT THE END OF THOSE TwO YEARS THAT WE WOULD SEE IF 
THE CIRCUMSTANCES OBLIGE FRANCE TO DEVELOP ATOMIC ENERGY IN BOTH 
(INDUSTRIAL AND MILITARY) DIRECTIONS.® 

HE SAID THERE ARE TWO PROJECTS WHICH CAN AND SHOULD BE UNDERTAKEN 
IMMEDIATELY WITH FRENCH SPONSORSHIP." A TRANSPORTATION COMMUNITY AND 
A POWER POOL, EVENTUALLY TO INCLUDE 4TOMIC ENERGY ALONG WITH ELECTRIC- 
ITY, GAS AND OIL.

APRIL 5 CAP)-PREMIER NGO DINH DIEM MOVED 
TODAY TO MEET OBJECTIONS RELIGIOUS AND POLITICAL SECTS TO HIS 
GOVERNMENT BY SETTING UP A HIGH POLITICAL COUNCIL. BUT THERE WERE Dousts 
THAT ITS ESTABLISHMENT WOULD SATISFY THE DISSIDENT GROUPS. 

THE SOUTH VIET NAM GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED IT WOULD CREATE THE NEW 
COUNCIL TO ADVISE THE PREMIER ON BROAD LINES OF POLICY. 

REPRESENTATIVES OF THE SECTS WOULD BE INCLUDED AMONG ITS MEMBERS. 

IT SEEMED PARTICULARLY UNLIKELY THAT SUCH A COUNCIL WOULD 
PLACATE THE BINH XUYEN SOCIETY, ONE OF THREE IMPORTANT DISSIDENT Groups, 
WHICH IS NOW IN ARMED REVOLT AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT. 

THE BINH XUYEN HAS DEMANDED ESTABLISHMENT OF A HIGH COUNCIL 
HOLDING SWEEPING EXECUTIVE POWER ON WHICH THE PREMIER WOULD BE ONLY 
ONE OF S QUAL MEMBERS. 

THE BINH XUYEN -- LIKE ITS ALLIES THE CAO DAI AND HOA HAO 
RELIGIOUS SECTS. -- CONTROLS ITS OWN PRIVATE ARMY. IT IS AN 
ORGANIZATION OF EX-RIVER PIRATES AND CONTROLS THE VICE IN SAIGON. 

DIEM SAID HE WOULD BEGIN CONSULTATIONS SOON ON MAKEUP OF THE 
COUNCIL. IN AN OFFICIAL COMMUNIQUE, THE GOVERNMENT SAID: 

“IN ORDER TO PERMIT THE VARIOUS LEVELS OF THE POPULATION TO 
PARTICIPATE MORE AND MORE IN THE DIRECTION OF THE AFFAIRS OF STATE,

(100) WASHINGTON, APRIL 5 (AP)-THE GOVERNMENT OF PERU AND THE WORLD 
BANK TODAY SIGNED AN 18 MILLION DOLLAR LOAN FOR A GIANT IRRIGATION 
PROJECT, FIRST ENVISIONED BY THE INCA INDIANS CENTURIES AGO. 

THE FIRST PHASE OF THE 50 MILLION DOLLAR PROJECT WAS COMPLETED By 
THE PERUVIAN GOVERNMENT, WITHOUT OUTSIDE HELP, IN 1953. IT PUT 40,000 
ACRES OF NEW LAND UNDER’ IRRIGATION. THE SECOND PHASE WILL ADD 125,000 

SOME OF THE ORIGINAL IRRIGATION WORKS BUILT BY THE ANCIENT INCA 
CIVILIZATION ALREADY HAVE BEEN PUT TO USE IN THE PROJECT. IT IS AIMED 
AT INCREASING PERU'S FOOD SUPPLY, DEVELOPING A RICH BUT ARID REGION IN 
NORTHERN PERU, IN PRODUCING LONG STAPLE COTTON FOR EXPORT, AND CREATING 
A NEW GROUP OF FARM OWNERS.

MACARTHUR-YALTA (700) 

NEW YORK, APRIL 5 CAP)-FOR THE SECOND TIME IN A WEEK, GEN. DOUGLAS 
MACARTHUR'S AIDE TONIGHT BITTERLY DENOUNCED A PUBLISHED REPORT THAT 
HIS CHIEF FAVORED CONCESSIONS TO RUSSIA TO GET HER INTO THE 
WAR AGAINST JAPAN IN 1945. 

“NO COMPETENT EVIDENCE WHATSOEVER EXISTS*® TO SUPPORT THE VIEW 


THAT CONCESSIONS TO RUSSIA AT THE YALTA CONFERENCE STEMMED IN PART FROM 


MACARTHUR'S ADVICE, SAID MAJe GENe COURTNEY WHITNEY. 

WHITNEY'S STATEMENT REPLIED TO AN ARTICLE IN THE CURRENT ISSUE 
OF THE REPORTER MAGAZINE BY LOUIS MORTON, CHIEF OF THE PACIFIC 
SECTION OF THF ARMY'S OFFICE OF MILITARV HISTORY. 


MORTON WROTE THAT MACARTHUR "STATED EMPHATICALLY AT THE TIME 
OF YALTA TO MORE THAN ONE VISITOR THAT AMERICAN FORCES SHOULD NOT 
aE eT APAN UNTIL THREE MONTHS AFTER THE RED ARMY ATTACKED IN 
MORTON ADDED THAT MACARTHUR TOLD VISITORS--WHOM MORTON DID NOT 
IDENTIFY--THAT MACARTHUR UNDERSTOOD STALIN WOULD ASK _A PRICE FOR 
GOING TO WAR AGAINST JAPAN AND THAT MACARTHUR “WAS PERFECTLY WILLING 
TO MAKE SUCH CONCESSIONS." 

WHITNEY CITED A PASSAGE IN A BOOK BY CORNELIUS VANDERBILT WHITNEY, 
WHO ACCOMPANIED THE LATE NAVY SECRETARY JAMES Ve FORRESTAL TO A 
MEETING WITH MACARTHUR IN THE PHILIPPINES IN FEBRUARY, 1945. 

WHITNEY SAID CORNELIUS VANDERBILT WHITNEY'S ACCOUNT OF THE 
MEETING "SHOULD DEMOLISH THE SPURIOUS EFFORTS BEING MADE TO POISON 
THE PUBLIC MIND BY THE INJECTION OF FALSE AND IRRELEVENT EVIDENCE 
IN THE CURRENT DISCUSSIONS." 

THE MAIN EVIDENCE THAT MACARTHUR DID FAVOR RUSSIAN ENTRY AGAINST 
JAPAN IS IN FORRESTAL'S DIARY. IT SAYS8 

*HE (MACARTHUR) FELT THAT WE SHOULD SECURE THE COMMITMENT OF THE 
RUSSIANS TO ACTIVE AND VIGOROUS PROSECUTION AGAINST THE JAPANESEs.. 
HE EXPRESSED DOUBT THAT ANYTHING LESS THAN 60 DIVISIONS BY THE RUSSIANS 
WOULD BE SUFFICIENT.®

TOKYO, APRIL 6 (AP)-JAPANESE SCIENTISTS LAST NIGHT REPORTED FINDING 
"HOT RAIN® ISOTOPES INDICATING THAT THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA BOTH 
EXPLODED THERMONUCLEAR BOMBS COATED WITH URANIUM JACKETS IN 1954. 

SCIENTISTS SAY A URANIUM JACKET AROUND A HYDROGEN BOMB WOULD BOOST 
ITS KILLING POWER MANY TIMES. 

TWO SCIENTISTS SAID THEY HAD DISCOVERED ISOTOPES OF URANIUM 237 
AND PLUTONIUM 239 IN DUST AND RAINFALL COLLECTED LAST MAY AND 
SEPTEMBER IN JAPAN. 

THEY SAID THE ISOTOPES IN MAY PROBABLY CAME FROM U.S. TESTS AT 
BIKINI; THOSE IN SEPTEMBER FROM SOVIET TESTS IN SIBERIA. 

DRe YUSUKE YOKOYAMA OF TOKYO UNIVERSITY SAID BOTH ISOTOPES WOULD 
RESULT FROM THE EXPLOSION OF A NATURAL URANIUM JACKET AROUND A 
TERMONUCLEAR BOMB. 

PROF. SEITARO ODA OF NIIGATA UNIVERSITY SUPPORTED YOKOYAMA'S 
REPORT. HE SAID HE HAD DISCOVERED THE ISOTOPES INDEPENDENTUYyI Is 
ANALYSES OF DUST AND RAIN IN MAY AND SEPTEMBER. Pd 

THE REPORTS WERE MADE TO A CONFERENCE OF MORE THAN 20 
JAPANESE SCIENTISTS CALLED TO COORDINATE FINDINGS ON RADIOACTIVE RAIN. 

THE UeS. TEST ON MARCH 1, 1954, AT THE BIKINI ATOLL PROVING GROUND 
SURPRISED OBSERVERS AT THE EXTENT OF RADIOACTIVE FALLOUT. JAPANESE 
FISHERMEN ON THE LUCKY DRAGON, ABOUT 80 MILES AWAY, WERE DUSTED WITH 
RADIOACTIVE ASH. THEY WERE CONFINED TO A HOSPITAL LONG AFTER THEIR 
RETURN TO JAPAN, 

ONE OF THE FISHERMEN DIED. JAPANESE AND U.S. DOCTORS AND, OFFICIALS 
HAVE DISPUTED WHETHER THE DEATH WAS CAUSED BY RADIATION EFFECTS OR A 
LIVER AILMENT,

FIRST LEAD AUSTRIAN (160) 

VIENNA, APRIL 6 (AP)-THE AUSTRIAN GOVERNMENT SAID TODAY THE 
PURPOSE OF CHANCELLOR JULIUS RAAB'S VISIT TO MOSCOW NEXT WEEK IS 
TO BRING THE BIG FOUR POWERS BACK TO THE CONFERENCE TABLE. 

RAAB HAS BEEN INVITED BY THE SOVIETS TO DISCUSS THE LONG- 
DELAYED STATE TREATY. 

THE WESTERN POWERS DECLARED JOINTLY THAT A BIG FOUR AMBASSADORS' 
CONFERENCE COULD TAKE PLACE SOON IF MOSCOW OFFERS RAAB PROPOSALS 
WHICH "HOLD CLEAR PROMISE" OF RESTORING AUSTRIAN INDEPENDENCE. 


RAAB'S OFFICE JSSUED AN OFFICIAL STATEMENT SAYING IT WAS SATISFIED 
WITH THE WEST'S DECLRATION. 


+ tc ei 





THE DECLARATION "ABOVE ALL CONTRADICTS REPORTS.««THAT 
THE THREE WESTERN ALLIES ARE AGAINST HOLDING A CONFERENCE ON THE 
AUSTRIAN TREATY," THE STATEMENT ADDED. 

THHE STATEMENT SAID AUSTRIA NEVER DOUBTED THE WESTERN POWERS 
WERE ALWAYS PREPARED TO BRING THIS COUNTRY FREEDOM AND THE TRIP OF 
THE AUSTRIAN DELEGATION TO MOSCOW "IS A SUITABLE STEP TOWARD 
REACHING THIS AIM." j | 

AUSTRIA, THE STATEMENT ADDED, KNOWS A TREATY CAN ONLY BE SIGNED BY 
AGREEMENT AMONG THE BIG FOUR. 

VIENNESE NEWSPAPERS SAID AUSTRIA WILL MAKE NO SECRET 
AGREEMENTS WITH RUSSIA WHEN RAAB FLIES TO MOSCOW. 

WHILE THE WEST'S STATEMENT WAS GREETED WITH ENTHUSIASM BY THE 
JIENNA PRESS, THE PAPERS WARNED THAT IT WOULD NOT MAKE THINGS EASY 
FOR RAAB. THEY POINTED TO A MOSCOW RADIO STATEMENT THIS MORNING 
THAT THE WEST'S DECLARATION "WILL LIMIT RAAB'S MISSION AND MAKE 
IMPOSSIBLE A POSITIVE RESULT." 

“THIS (RADIO MOSCOW) COMMENT MAKES IT APPEAR PROBABLE THAT THE 
SOVJET UNION INTENDS NOT ONLY TO CLARIFY ITS ATTITUDE TOWARD THE 
STATE TREATY AND |TO EXPRESS ITS FURTHER WISHES, BUT WANTS TO GAIN 
OTHER ENDS, TOO," SAID THE INDEPENDENT NEUE KURIER« 

“WHAT AIMS CAN THESE BE?" IT ASKED. “PERHAPS THAT AUSTRIA MAKES A 
SEPARATE AGREEMENT AND ENTERS INTO SECRET CLAUSES. WE CANNOT BELIEVE 
THIS. BUT IF SUCH INTENTIONS EXIST, THE EXPERIENCE OF HUNGARY, 
CZECHOSLOVAKIA AND OTHER SOVIET SATELLITES TEACH US THAT AUSTRIA 

NOT GO THIS WAY. 
Ca TETRA BOULD GAIN NOTHING BUT THAT ITS PRESENT SITUATION OF INNER 
FREEDOM, DESPITE OCCUPATION, WOULD BE EXCHANGED FOR THE LOSS OF BOTH 
INNER AND EXTERNAL FREEDOM,* THE NEUE KURIER SAID. 

THE INDEPENDENT DIE PRESSE SAID THAT THE WESTERN DECLARATION WAS 
RECFIVED WITH SATISFACTION IN THE AUSTRIAN CHANCELLERY. 

AN OFFICIAL REACTION FROM RAAB'S OFFICE WAS EXPECTED LATER TODAY. 

THE INDEPENDENT BILD TELEGRAF POINTED OUT THAT A MAJOR DIFFERENCE 
BETWEEN EAST AND WEST WAS ON THE QUESTION OF AUSTRIAN NEUTRALITY.

. WASHINGTON APRIL 7 CAP)-THE COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION TODAY DECLINED 
TO DELETE ONE’OF THE ISSUES IN THE EDWARD LAMB HEARING. 

THE 6, 1/2-MONTH-HEARING, NOW IN RECESS, IS AON ALLEGATIONS THAT 
LAMB, A TOLEDO, OHIO, LAWYER, PUBLISHER AND BROADCASTER, ONCE KNOWINGLY 
ASSOCIATED WITH COMMUNISTS. 

LAMB, WHO IS SEEKING RENEWAL OF LICENSE FOR HIS ERIE, PAs, TELEVISION 
STATION, WICU, HAS DENIED THE ALLEGATIONS AND HAS ACCUSED COMMISSION 
INVESTIGATORS OF HAVING TRIED TO INDUCE WITNESSES TO TESTIFY FALSELY 

IT WAS THE FALSE-TESTIMONY ALLEGATION THAT LAMB HAD ASKED TO BE 
DELETED. HE SAID IT WAS AN ISSUE WHICH HE BROUGHT UP IN A COURT 
PROCEEDING AND THEREFORE HAD NO PLACE IN THE COMMISSION HEARING. 

THE COMMISSION SAID TODAY THE ISSUE CONCERNS "GRAVE CHARGES® WHICH 
IT FEELS ARE "DIRECTLY RELATED" TO THE CASE AND THEREFORE SHOULD BE 
CONSIDERED BY_THE EXAMINER. 

THUS FAR THE HEARING HAS BEEN CONCERNED ONLY WITH THE FIRST ISsuF-- 
WHETHER LAMB MADE ANY FALSE STATEMENTS OR MISREPRESENTATIONS IN NON- 
COMMUNIST AFFIDAVITS PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TO THE COMMISSION. 

LAMB HAS SAID THE AFFIDAVITS WERE TRUE AND HAS OFFERED $10,000 
TO ANYONE WHO CAN PROVE THEY WERE FALSE. 

THE HEARING IS SCHEDULED TO RESUME APRIL 18.

MOSCOW, APRIL 9 CAP) “THE SOVIET UNION DECLARED TODAY IT CONSIDERS 
UNJUSTIFIED ANY FURTHER DELAY IN AN AUSTRIAN INDEPENDENCE TREATY ANp 
EXPRESSED HOPE THE VISIT HERE NEXT WEEK OF CHANCELLOR JULIUS RAAB 
WILL PROMOTE A SPEEDY CONCLUSION OF THE LONG*DELAYED TREATY. 

APPARENTLY TAKING NOTE OF A DECLARATION ON TUESDAY BY THE THREE 
WESTERN POWERS THAT THE AUSTRIAN TREATY WAS A MATTER OF FOUR-POWER 
CONCERN, SOVIET FOREIGN MINISTER Ve Me MOLOTOV CALLED IN THE 
DIPLOMATIC REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN AND FRANCE 
AND PRESENTED THEM IDENTICAL STATEMENTS.» 

. THESE SAID THE SOVIET UNION TOOK INTO CONSIDERATION THAT AUSTRIAN 
OFFICIALS HAVE EXCHANGED OPINIONS ON THE TREATY WITH THE WESTERN 
POWERS SINCE THE FOUR-POWER FOREIGN MINISTERS' CONFERENCE IN BERLIN 
EARLY IN 1954.6 | 

“THE SOVIET. UNION EXPRESSES THE HOPE THAT IN CASE THERE IS A 
DESIRE ON THE PART OF ALL STATES CONCERNED, IT WILL BE POSSIBLE TO 
ACHIEVE AN AGREEMENT FOR THE CONCLUSION OF AN AUSTRIAN STATE TREATY," 
THE STATEMENTS ADDED. 

SINCE THE END OF WORLD WAR II THE FOREIGN MINISTERS OF THE FOUR 
POWERS HAVE HAD 15 SESSIONS DEVOTED TO AN AUSTRIAN TREATY WITHOUT 
REACHING ANY SUCCESSFUL CONCLUSIONe THEIR DEPUTIES HAVE ATTENDED 
©60 SESSIONS TRYING TO FIND COMMON GROUND ON WHICH THEIR CHIEFS COULD 
WORK OUT AN AGREEMENT. | 

A FINAL STUMBLING BLOCK HAS BEEN AGREEMENT OVER THE TIME FOR 
WITHDRAWAL OF OCCUPATION TROOPS~~44,900 RUSSIAN AND 23,000 OF THE 
WESTERN POWERSe &gt;) | a ( 

AT THE BERLIN CONFERENCE THE RUSSIANS LINKED WITHDRAWAL OF TROOPS 
WITH THE CONCLUSION OF A PEACE TREATY FOR GERMANY. TODAY S 
STATEMENT TO THE WESTERN POWERS SAID THE RUSSIANS HAD PROPOSED AT 
BERLIN ®TO RETURN NOT LATER THAN IN 1955 TO THE EXAMINATION OF 
THE QUESTION REGARDING THE TIME OF WITHDRAWING THE TROOPS OF THE 
FOUR POWERS FROM AUSTRIAN TERRITORY." . 

THE STATEMENTS RECALLED THE SOVIET PROPOSAL OF LAST AUGUST FOR A 
FOUR-POWER MEETING ON THE AMBASSADORIAL LEVEL IN VIENNA TO DISCUSS 
AN AUSTRIAN TREATYe er 

IT ADDED THAT "UNFORTUNATELY® THIS WAS NOT CONVENED, AND THE 
SOVIET UNION, ®CONSIDERING AS UNJUSTIFIED ANY FURTHER DELAY IN THE 
MATTER OF CONCLUDING THE AUSTRIAN STATE TREATY," PUT FORWARD ITS 


NEW PROPOSALS OF LAST FEBe Se 





~ THESE WERE AIMED, THE SOVIET UNION DECLARED, "AT PUTTING AN END 
TO THE PRESENT ABNORMAL SITUATION WHEN THE QUESTION REGARDING A 
STATE TREATY WITH AUSTRIA HAS NOT YET BEEN SETTLED AND AUSTRIA, 
10 YEARS AFTER HER LIBERATION FROM HITLERITE RULE, STILL CONTINUES 
TO REMAIN UNDER THE CONTROL OF OCCUPATION AUTHORITIES OF THE FOUR 


POWERS."

BY JOHN RODERICK 

SAIGON, SOUTH VIET NAM, APRIL 9 (AP)-PREMIER NGO DINE 
CONSULTATIONS TODAY WITH THE LEADERS OF SOUTH VIET NAM'S MANY 
POLITICAL PARTIES TO FORM A HIGH POLITICAL COUNCIL WHICH WILL DRAW 
UP THE BROAD LINESOF THE GOVERNMENT'S FUTURE PROGRAM. 

THE COUNCIL IS AN INNOVATION ENVISAGED BY THE PREMIER AS AN 
ANSWER TO THE DEMANDS OF POLITICO-RELIGIOUS AND MILITARY GROUPS. 
IT WILL SERVE AS A CONSULTATIVE AND ADVISORY BODY IN ADDITION TO 
THE REGULAR CABINET, WHICH DIEM ALSO PLANS TO REVISE SOON. 

AMONG THE 23 PARTY LEADERS WHO MET WITH THE PREMIER AT INDEPENDENCE 
PALANCE, WERE LE PHUC THIEN, MEMBER OF THE NATIONAL RESTORATION 
PARTY, AND LE KHAC HOAI, OF THE NATIONAL RESISTANCE FRONT. BOTH 
OUTSTANDING NATIONALISTS. THE SOCIALIST PARTY AND THE REVOLUTIONARY 
DAI VIET, WHICH HAVE BEEN IN DIEM'S OPPOSITION, ALSO WERE REPRESENTED. 

CONSULTATIONS WILL CONTINUE NEXT WEEK. THE’COUNCIL. ONCE CREATED, 
IS EXPECTED TO SATISFY THE NEED FOR WIDER REPRESENTATION IN THE DIEM 
GOVERNMENT AND LEAVE THE PREMIER FREE TO CHOOSE NONPARTISAN, NON- 
SECTARIAN TECHNICIANS FOR THE ACTUAL CABINET POSTS. 

IN HIS WELCOMING SPEECH DIEM SAID HE WAS CONVINCED THAT THE 
PARTIES WOULD BE WILLING TO HELP IN THE RECONSTRUCTION OF THE COUNTRY 
AND GIVE THE BENEFIT OF THEIR EXPERIENCE TO THE GOVERNMENT, 

THE TACIT TRUCE AGREED UPON BY THE GOVERNMENT AND THE BINH 
XUYEN SOCIETY CONTINUES, BUT THE POLITICAL WARFARE BETWEEN THE Two 
REMAINS JUST AS ACUTE AS EVER. A PLASTIC BOMB WAS TOSSED AT HEAD- 
QUARTERS OF THE HOA HAO RELIGIOUS SECT, WHICH HAS BEEN SIDING 
WITH THE BINH XUYEN, THIS MORNING. BUT THERE WAS NO ONE IN THE 
BUILDING IN THE HEART OF SAIGON AND NO DAMAGE WAS DONE. 

THE BINH XUYEN PROMPTLY ACCUSED THE PREMIER OF HAVING 
INSTIGATED THE BOMBING. IT ALSO COMPLAINED OF THE KIDNAPPINGS oF 
HAO HAO AND BINH XUYEN MILITANTS, WHICH PRESUMABLY REFERS To 
INCREASING DESERTIONS IN THE BINH XUYEN RANKS.

TOKYO, APRIL 9 (AP)-JAPAN TODAY AGREED TO PAY THAILAND THE EQUIVA- 
LENT OF APPROXIMATELY 41 1/2 MILLION DOLLARS IN CASH, GOODS AND SERVICES 
TO SETTLE A 375 MILLION DOLLAR WORLD WAR II CLAIM. 

A SPECIAL THAI DELEGATION ACCEPTED THE TERMS, THE JAPANESE FOREIGN 
OFFICE ANNOUNCED. 


THE AGREEMENT CALLS FOR A CASH PAYMENT IN POUNDS STERLING OF 15 
MILLION DOLLARS IN FIVE ANNUAL INSTALLMENTS. | 

IT SPECIFIES THAT "UP TO 9,600 MILLION YEN" $26,666,666) WILL BE 
PAID IN “CAPITAL GOODS OF JAPAN AND SERVICES OF THE JAPANESE PEOPLE 
IN THE FORM OF INVESTMENT AND/OR CREDIT.® 

TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THIS NON-CASH PART OF THE PAYMENT ARE SUB- 
JECT TO LATER NEGOTIATIN« reiidieanttatis ci 

THE DEBT STEMS’FROM A 1,500 MILLION BHAT (375 MILLION DOLLARS) 
ADVANCE THAILAND MADE WHILE OCCUPIED BY JAPAN DURING WORLD WAR 11. 
JAPAN FOR A TIME CLAIMED IT OWED NOTHING, LATER OFFERED TO PAY UP TO

LT. COL. EDWARD E. AYER OF MCCLUSKY, NeDey DIVISION G-1 (PERSONNEL), 
HAMMERED OUT THE TRAVEL DETAILS FOR THE 1ST. 

"WE STARTED FROM SCRATCH," MAYER SAID, "BUT NOW WE BELIEVE WE'VE 
JUST ABOUT GOT IT LICKED. GRATING WAS A’BIG PROBLEM. EACH FAMILY 
WILL HAVE AT LEAST TWO TONS OF PERSONAL BELONGINGS, UNMARRIED GI$ 
SEVERAL HUNDRED POUNDS EACH." 

MAYER SAID THE ARMY AT FIRST DECIDED THAT FAMILY PETS AND UNIT 
MASCOTS, INCLUDING MONKEYS AND PARROTS, WOULD HAVE TO BE LEFT BEHIND. 

“BUT THERE WAS SUCH A PROTEST," MAYER SAID, "THAT THE ARMY 
CHANGED ITS MIND. PETS AND MASCOTS WILL COME ALONG, BUT AT THE 
EXPENSE OF THE OWNERS." 

REGULAR ARMY SOLDIERS BENEFIT MOST FROM "GYROSCOPE," MAYER SAID. 

"THEY WILL GET TO TRAVEL WITH THEIR WIVES AND FAMILIES, THERE WILL 
BE BETTER CHANCES FOR PROMOTION, AND MORE EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES. 


ALL OF THESE BOOST MORALE.”

BERLIN, APRIL 10 (AP)-THE COMMUNISTS BEGAN MAKING POLITICAL CAPITAL 
TODAY OUT OF A YOUTHFUL SOVIET RUNAWAY WHO DECIDED HE PREFERRED LIFE 
BEHIND THE IRON CURTAIN. 

THE TEENAGED YOUTH--VALERY LYSIKOV, SON OF A SOVIET AIR FORCE 
LIEUTENANT COLONEL STATIONED OUTSIDE EAST BERLIN--WAS RETURNED TO HIS 
PARENTS YESTERDAY BY UeS. OFFICIALS. HE CROSSED INTO WEST BERLIN 
MARCH 18 AND ASKED FOR ASYLUM, SAYING HE WAS TIRED OF LIFE UNDER CON- 
MUNISMe BUT AFTER THREE WEEKS HE CHANGED HIS MIND AND SAID HE WANTED 
TO GO BACKe 

TODAY, THE COMMUNIST EAST GERMAN BERLINER ZEITUNG PUBLISHED A SAR- 
CASTIC CARTOON. IT SHOWED A VICIOUS-LOOKING CRIMINAL BEING RELEASED 
FROM SING SING. A CELLMATE SHOWS SURPRISE, AND ASKS:

NEW DELHI, INDIA ana 10 (AP)-PRIME MINISTER NEHRU AND FOREIGN 
MINISTER PHAM VAN DONG COMMUNIST NORTH VIET NAM TODAY CONCLUDED 
THREE DAYS OF TALKS ON INDOCHINA. A COMMUNIQUE SAID THEY “AGREED ON 
THE IMPORTANCE OF FREE ELECTIONS AND THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE UNITY OF 
VIET NAM AS PROVIDED AT GENEVA." 

THE CENEVA ARMISTICE, WHICH HALTED THE INDOCHINA WAR AND SPLIT VIET 
NAM, CALLED FOR A VOTE IN 1956 TO DETERMINE WHETHER ALL THE COUNTRY 
SHOULD BE CONTROLLED BY THE COMMUNIST NORTH OR THE WESTERN-SUPPORTED 
DEGIME IN THE SOUTH. INDIA HEADS THE INTERNATIONAL TRUCE COMMISSION 
SUPERVISING THE AGREEMENT» __ 

THE JOINT STATEMENT BY NEHRU AND DONG SAID THE COMMISSION HAD PRO- 
DUCED "GOOD RESULTS" AND ADDED THAT FUTURE DIFFICULTIES COULD BE RE- 
SOLVED "BY SUSTAINED ENDEAVOR AND IN A SPIRIT OF GOOD WILL." THE Two 
TEADERS PLEDGED THEMSELVES TO WORK TOWARD SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION 
OF THE GENEVA AGREEMENTS “BOTH IN THEIR TERMS AND SPIRIT." 

NEHRU AND DONG ADDED THAT THEY WERE “GRATIFIED AT THE FRIENDSHIP 
BETWEEN THEIR TWO COUNTRIES* AND THEY FELT IT HAD BEEN STRENGTHENED py 
THE NEW DELHI MEETING.

(650) EISENHOWER-FORMOSA--BUDGET 
BY JACK BELL | 

WASHINGTON, APRIL 10 (AP)-PRESIDENT EIDENHOWER IS REPORTED TO HAVE 
DIRECTED AMERICAN FORCES TO STAND CLEAR OF FIGHTING THAT MIGHT 
BREAK OUT IN THE FORMOSA AREA UNTIL HE CAN ASSESS THE EXTENT 
AND INTENT OF ANY INITIAL CHINESE COMMUNIST ATTACK. 

THE PRESIDENT IS REPRESENTED BY PERSONS VERSED IN THE ADMINISTRaA- 
TION'S FAR EASTERN POLICIES AS HAVING INFORMED THE CHINESE NATIONAL- 
ISTS THEY HOLD THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR DEFENDING NOT ONLY 
QUEMOY AND MATSU BUT FORMOSA ITSELF. ol 

EISENHOWER'S PRESENT POSITION WAS SUMMED UP THIS WAY: 

THE NATIONALISTS, WHO HAVE BEEN GIVEN THE LATEST TYPES OF 
AMERICAN FIGHTING EQUIPMENT SHORT OF NUCLEAR WEAPONS, WILL BE 
EXPECTED TO BEAR ALONE THE INITIAL THRUSTS OF ANY ATTACK--MASSIVE 
OR OTHERWISE--THAT DEVELOPS. THERE IS A STRONG FEELING WITHIN THE AD- 
MINISTRATION THAT CHIANG KAI SHEK'S MEN CAN HANDLE ANYTHING SHORT OF 
AN ALL-OUT INVASION. 

AMERICAN FORCES WOULD STAND IN READINESS OUTSIDE THE RANGE OF 
BATTLE. THEY WOULD NOT JOIN IN THE FIRING UNLESS DELIBERATELY 
ATTACKED. 

IF EISENHOWER DECIDES THE NATIONALISTS CAN'T REPEL THE REDS 
ALONE, HIS DECISION ON AMERICAN INTERVENTION WILL BE BASED ON THE 
BEST Ue Se EVALUATION OF COMMUNIST INTENTIONS AT THE TIME. 

Ix THE COMMUNISTS SHOULD CHANGE THEIR PROPAGANDA LINE BY 
ANNOUNCING PUBLICLY THEY WANT ONLY QUEMOY AND MATSU, EISENHOWER WOULD 
HAVE TO CONSIDER WORLD OPINION AND THE LIKELY OPPOS{TION OF AMERICA'S 
\LLIES TOWARD DEFENDING THE COASTAL ISLANDS UNDER THOSE CIRCUMSTANCES. 

IF THE PRESIDENT IS CONVINCED, HOWEVER, THAT AN ASSAULT ON QUEMOY 
AND MATSU IS THE BEGINNING OF A MASSIVE EFFORT TO TAKE FORMOSA 
AMERICAN FORCES WOULD MOVE INTO ACTION WITH TACTICAL, SMALL SIZE 


ATOMIC WEAPONS. 

THERE WOULD BE NO EMPLOYMENT OF THE FUSION TYPE OF H=BOMB 
WITH ITS LETHAL FALLOUT OVER WIDE AREASe THE EFFORT WOULD BE TO 
POINT MILITARY TARGETS WITH THE LESS POWERFUL ATOMIC WEAPONS. 

THIS SUMMARIZATION REPRESENTS TODAY'S ADMINISTRATION TOP 
LEVEL THINKING ON THE DELICATE FORMOSA SITUATION, TWO WEEKS AND 
SECURITY COUNCIL MEETINGS AFTER THE PUBLIC FLAREUP OVER WHETHER 
MIGHT BREAK OUT IN THE FORMOSA AREA BY APRIL 15-6 J ea

(ADVANCE APRIL 10 (AP)-THE NATIONAL PLANNING ASSNey CITING "Fryr 
YEARS OF FUMBLING AND CHANOE," TODAY SUGGESTED THE U.S. TECHNICAL 
COOPERATION PROGRAM BE GIVEN PERMANENT, SEMI-AUTONOMOUS STATUS WITHIN 
THE STATE DEPARTMENTe 

THE PROGRAM, WHICH SUPPLIES "KNOW HOW" TO UNDERDEVELOPED NATIons, 
COSTS AROUND 120 MILLION DOLLARS A YEARe 

THE ASSOCIATION MADE ITS RECOMMENDATIONS AFTER A TWO-YEAR STUDY oF 
TECHNICAL COOPERATION IN LATIN AMERICA. THE STUDY WAS FINANCED WITH A 
$440,000 FORD FOUNDATION GRANT. THE ASSOCIATION ITSELF IS NON-POLITI- 


CALs 

ITS RECOMMENDATIONS, ALTHOUGH MADE ON THE BASIS OF LATIN 
EXPERIENCE, APPLY ON A GLOBAL SCALE. 

THE ASSOCIATION'S 25-MEMBER POLICY COMMITTEE, HEADED BY LAIRD BELL 
OF CHICAGO, NOTED THAT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE OR COOPERATION HAD HAD 
FOUR DIFFERENT ADMINISTRATIONS WITHIN THE PAST FIVE YEARS. 

FROM 1950 THROUGH 1953, THE PROGRAM WAS ADMINISTERED BY THE STATE 
DEPARTMENT. BUT FROM 1951 THROUGH 1953, COORDINATION WAS PROVIDED 
THROUGH THE DIRECTOR OF MUTUAL SECURITY. 

SINCE 1953, THE FOREIGN OPERATIONS ADMINISTRATION (FOA) HAS HAD THE 
RESPONSIBILITY, BUT FOA ALSO HAS ADMINISTERED MILITARY AID AND ECONOMIC 
ASSISTANCE. 

AFTER FOA EXPIRES ON JUNE 30, TECHNICAL COOPERATION IS SCHEDULED 
TO BE RETURNED TO THE STATE DEPARTMENT. 

THE PLANNING ASSOCIATION SAID THE RETURN COULD BE EFFECTIVE ONLY 
“IF THE DEPARTMENT GRANTS THIS AGENCY THE BROAD OPERATING FREEDOM AND 
THE RESPONSIBILITY NECESSARY." 

IT SUGGESTED THAT PERHAPS THE STATE DEPARTMENT COULD BE REORGANIZED 
INTO TWO MAIN BRANCHES. 

ONE WOULD DEAL WITH DIPLOMATIC AND CONSULAR ACTIVITIES. THE OTHER 
MIGHT ADMINISTER OVERSEAS ACTION PROGRAMS. TECHNICAL COOPERATION, THE 
ASSOCIATION SAID, SHOULD HAVE ITS OWN STAFFS AND CAREER OFFICERS, HEADED 
BY "A PERSON OF PRESTIGE AT HOME AND ABROAD." 

THE POLICY COMMITTEE ALSO RECOMMENDED THAT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AP- 
PROPRIATIONS SHOULD BE AUTHORIZED ANNUALLY, SO AS TO “REMOVE FROM THE 
PROGRAM THE MISLEADING APPEARANCE OF SHORT-RUN STATUS." 

THE PLANNING ASSOCIATION'S BOARD CHAIRMAN, HeCHRISTIAN SONNE, EM- 
PHASIZED AT A NEWS CONFERENCE THAT PUBLIC PROGRAMS OF TECHNICAL COOPER- 
ATION ARE A ®BASIC ELEMENT" IN THE NATION'S FOREIGN POLICY. _ | 

AT THE SAME TIME, HE SAID THERE WOULD BE LITTLE LIKELIHOOD OF IN- 
CREASED DEMANDS FOR FUNDS, SAYING IT WOULD BE DIFFICULT 
TO SPEND ANY MORE ON THE PROGRAM INTELLIGENTLY. ess

F MOSCOW, APRIL 11 (AP)-AUSTRIAN CHANCELLOR JULIUS RAAB ARRIVED IN 
MOSCOW IN’A BLINDING SNOWSTORM TODAY FOR TALKS AIMED AT BREAKING THE 
LONG EAST-WEST DEADLOCK OVER AN AUSTRIAN INDEPENDENCE TREATY. 

AUSTRIAN OFFICIALS SAID EXPLORATORY SOVIET-AUSTRIAN CONFERENCES 
WILL BEGIN TOMORROW AFTER RAAB HAS PAID KREMLIN COURTESY CALLS TO 
PREMIER MARSHAL NIKOLAI AeBULGANIN, PRESIDENT MARSHAL KLEMENTI Y. 
VOROSHILOV AND FOREIGN MINISTER VYACHESLAV M.MOLOTOV. THE CON- 
FERENCES ARE EXPECTED TO LAST ABOUT FOUR DAYS. | 

THE AUSTRIAN CHANCELLOR AND HIS 10-MEMBER DELEGATION ARRIVED IN TWO 
SPECIAL RUSSIAN PLANES. RAAB TOLD WELCOMERS HE WAS GLAD TO MAKE THE 
TRIP AND HOPED IT "WILL IMPROVE RELATIONS" BETWEEN RUSSIA AND AUSTRIA 
AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE "FORCES OF PEACE." HE NOTED THAT HIS ARRIVAL 
COINCIDED WITH THE 10TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE LIBERATION OF VIENNA FROM

SE THE FIRST CHIEF OF A NON-COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT TO VISIT MOSCOW SINCE 
THE WAR, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE PRESIDENT OF FINLAND. 

THE AUSTRIAN LEADER CAME ON MOLOTOV'S INVITATION. HE IS STAYING 
IN THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT GUEST HOUSE, NEXT DOOR TO THE AUSTRIAN

BY HENRY HARTZENBUSCH 1955 

MANILA, TUESDAY, APRIL 12 (AP)-TWO LEADING LEGISLATORS IN THIS 
STRONGLY ANTI-COMMONIST COUNTRY YESTERDAY SUPPORTED A VIEW THAT RED 
CHINA SHOULD BE ADMITTED TO THE UNITED NATIONS.» 

SEN. CLARO Me RECTO HAD OPENED DISCUSSION SUNDAY. HE SAID COMMUNIST 
CHINA’S ADMISSION TO THE UNITED NATIONS MIGHT CLEAR THE WAY FOR A 
PEACEFUL SOLUTION OF ASIAN PROBLEMS. 

SEN. JOSE Pe LAUREL, A NACIONALISTA PARTY ADMINISTRATION LEADER, 
SAID COMMUNIST CHINA'S ENTRY "WOULD NOT WORSEN TENSION IN THE FAR 
FASTe” HE SAID HE WAS NOT OPPOSED TO ADMISSION. 

JOSE Be LAUREL JRey SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES, SAID: 

WHILE = MAY NOT LIKE THE IDEA, THERE IS NO DENYING THE FACT THAT 
RED CHINESE GOVERNMENT IS RULING THE CHINESE MAINLAND. THE COMMUNIST 
CONOUEST OF THE CHINA MAINLAND IS AN ACCOMPLISHED FACT. "PERHAPS IT 
COULD BE BETTER FOR PEACE IN THE FAR EAST IF THE DEMOCRACIES SIT WITH 
THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS IN THE UNITED NATIONS." 

THE PHILIPPINE ADMINISTRATION UNDER PRESIDENT RAMON MAGSAYSAY HAS 
OPPOSED ANY RELATIONS WITH COMMUNIST CHINA OR RUSSIA. TRADE TO COMMUN- 
IST COUNTRIES IS BANNEDe OVERTURES INVITING THE PHILIPPINES TO VISIT 
RUSSIA HAVE BEEN TURNED DOWN. MAGSAYSAY HAS SUPPORTED PRESIDENT EISEN- 
HOWER*S POLICY OF DEFENDING FORMOSA AND THE PESCADORES AGAINST COMMUNIST 

CONGRESSIONAL LEADERS, HOWEVER, BEGAN DEMANDING A REAPPRAISAL OF THE 
FORMOSA POLICY LAST WEEKe MANY BELIEVE THE PHILIPPINES SHOULD REVISE 
ITS STAND, SINCE THE UNITED STATES APPEARS TO BE ALTERING ITS OWN 
POLICY. 

RECTO EXPRESSED THE BELIEF THAT THE UNITED STATES MIGHT WITHDRAW 
FROM ITS "FIRST LINE OF DEFENSE* IN ASIA, AND MOVE TO THE SO-CALLED 
"CANADIAN_LINE." THE "FIRST LINE OF DEFENSE" EXTENDS FROM NORTH OF 
JAPAN THROUGH OKINAWA, FORMOSA AND THE PHILIPPINES. 

THE AMERICAN-OWNED MANILA BULLETIN SAID RECTO'S VIEWS "IF TRUE, 

WOULD BE VERY ALARMING." : 

THE NEWSPAPER SAID IN AN EDITORIALS 

"THE NATIONAL POLICY OF THE PHILIPPINES WOULD HAVE TO BE COMPLETELY 
CHANGED IN DIRECTION AND PURPOSE. WE WOULD HAVE TO TURN AWAY FROM THE 
UNITED STATES AND INDULGE IN OUTRIGHT APPEASEMENT OF RED CHINA BY 
GIVING HER A SHOULDER UP INTO THE UNITED NATIONS AND OPENING CHANNELS 


OF TRADE AND COMMERCE.”

NEW YORK, APRIL 11 (AP)-ADM ARTHUR RADFORD, CHAIRMAN OF THE 
CHIEF s OF starr, SAID TONIGHT RUSSIA HAS SURGED FORWARD IN THE FiLn, 
Jk Ww e 

"OUR NATIONAL AIR POWER IS SECOND TO NONE," RADFORD SAID, "BUT 
I CANNOT GUARANTEE THIS WILL ALWAYS BE THE CASE...WE MUST &amp;UARD 
AGAINST COMPLACENCY ABOUT OUR TECHNOLOGICAL SUPERIORITY, AS THOUGH 
HAVING IT IS A FOREGONE CONCLUSION.” 

RADFORD SAID "OUR LATEST REPORTS INDICATE THAT SOVIET SCIENTIFIC 
TECHNOLOGICAL AND PRODUCTION SKILLS DEFINITELY HAVE SURGED FORWARD.* 

PRESENT UsS. MILITARY THINKING, HE STATED, IS TO PROVIDE "A STURDY 
BUT FLEXIBLE COMBINATION OF LAND, SEA, AMPHIBIOUS AND AIR FORCES." 

WITHIN THIS PATTERN,*® HE SAID, "OUR MILITARY FORCES ARE PREPARED, 
IF NECESSARY, TO USE NUCLEAR WEAPONS. BUT THIS DOES NOT COMMIT 
US TO SOLE RELIANCE ON NUCLEAR WEAPONS. PLANES THAT CAN CARRY ATOMIC 
BOMBS CAN ALSO CARRY CONVENTIONAL BOMBS. : 

"IN OTHER WORDS, EMPHASIS IS ON THE ABILITY TO APPLY QUICKLY 
WHATEVER FORCE IS REQUIRED TO STOP ANY KIND OF AGGRESSION WHERE IT 
STARTS--AT ITS SOURCE--BEFORE IT CAN EXPAND INTO A’ GLOBAL WAR." 

THE ADMIRAL SAID NATIONAL POLICY IS "TO PROVIDE FOR THE WELFARE AND 
SECURITY OF THE UNITED STATES THROUGH PEACE-- NOT WARees 

"BUT UNFORTUNATELY WE CANNOT BE CERTAIN WHAT THE COMMUNISTS WILL 
DO. WE CAN ONLY BE SURE THAT, LIKE ALL AGGRESSORS, THEY ARE LIKELY 
TO’ STRIKE WITHOUT WARNING. 

"WE WILL NOT COMMIT AN AGGRESSION," HE SAID. 

RADFORD SPOKE AT THE ANNUAL AWARDS HINNER OF AVIATORS POST 743 OF

MANILA, APRIL 12 CAP)-CONGRESSIONAL QUARTERS TODAY CRITICIZED THE 
APPOINTMENT OF GENe CARLOS Pe ROMULO AS HEAD OF THE PHILIPPINE DELE- 
GATION TO THE AFRO-ASIAN CONFERENCE AT BANDUNG, INDONESIA. 

SENe FRANCISCO Ae DELGADO, NACIONALISTA PARTY CHAIRMAN OF THE 
SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS COMMITTEE, SAID HIS FELLOW NACIONALISTA 
SENATOR. CLARO Me RECTO, SHOULD BE NAMED CO-LEADER OF THE DELEGATION. 

DELGADO DESCRIBED RECTO WHO HAS BEEN A POLITICAL ENEMY OF PRESI- 
DENT RAMON MAGSAYSAY'’S PERSONAL ENVOY TO THE UNITED STATES FOR YEARS, 
AS TEE "VOICE OF ASIA." 

ROMULO, HE CHARGED, IS THE “VOICE OF AMERICA." 

SENATE PRESIDENT EULOGIO RODRIGUES, SRe, WHO ALSO HEADS THE NACICN- 
ALISTA PARTY, REFUSED TO MAKE A CHANGE IN THE APPOINTMENT, SAYING A NON- 
PARTISAN GROUP THAT ADVISES PRESIDENT MAGSAYSAY HAD APPROVED IT. 

RODRIGUEZ POINTED OUT IT WAS RECTO HIMSELF WHO HAD PROPOSED ROMULO 
TO HEAD THE DELEGATIONe RECTO RETORTED TODAY THAT HE SUGGESTED ROMULO 
BEFORE HE KNEW “ROMULO WOULD REPRESENT AMERICA AT THE BANDUNG MEETING.” 

ROMULO ARRIVED HERE TODAY AND CONFERRED IMMEDIATELY WITH MAGSAYSAY 
ON THE BANDUNG CONFERENCE. RANKING LEADERS OF THE MAJOR POLITICAL 
PARTIES HAVE BEEN INVITED TO A CONFERENCE WEDNESDAY TO DISCUSS THE 
POSITION THE PHILIPPINES WILL TAKE ON MAJOR ISSUES THAT MAY ARISE 
AT BANDUNG, WHERE 29 ASIAN AND AFRICAN NATIONS MEET APRIL 18-24.

EGYPTIAN PREMIER GAMAL ABDEL NASSER A NOISY WELCOME TODAY. POLICE 
WIELDED STEEL-TIPPED BAMBOO STICKS TO KEEP THE PUSHING SPECTATORS 
FROM BREAKING THROUGH SAFETY BARRIERS AT THE AIRPORT.

PRIME MINISTER NEHRU IN ADVANCE OF THE AFRICAN-ASIAN CONFERENE OPENING 
IN BANDUNG, INDONESIA, NEXT MONDAY.

(ADVANCE) eeKASTORIA, GREECE, APRIL 12 CAP)-"“PERHAPS WE WOULD LIKE 
SOME CARAMELS,” SAID THE ROMANIAN COMMUNIST TEACHER. 

THE GREEK ¢HILDREN SITTING ON A BLANKET IN THE COURTYARD OF A 
SCHOOL IN BUCHAREST CAORUSED EAGER ASSENT. 

“ALL RIGHT," SAID THE TEACHER. “WHY DON'T YOU TRY PRAYING TO GOD 


FOR YOUR CARAMELS?" 
UNDER HER DIRECTION, THE CHILDREN PRAYED TO GODe NOTHING HAPPENED. 
“WE SHALL PRAY TO LENIN FOR CARAMELS."* 


*NOW." SAID THE TEACHER 
THE CHILDREN DID AS THEY WERE TOLD. AS IF BY MAGIC, CARAMELS 


SHOWERED ON THEM FROM THE WINDOWS OF THE SCHOOL. 

THAT WAS THE BEGINNING OF COMMUNIST INDOCTRINATION FOR THIS GROUP 
OF CHILDREN, NEWLY ABDUCTED FROM THEIR HOMELAND DURING THE GREEK 
CIVIL WAR OF 1948. 

THESE CHILDREN, AND MANY THOUSANDS LIKE THEM, WERE SELECTED FOR 
SPECIAL PAMPERING, FOR TREATMENT FAR BEYOND WHAT A ROMANIAN CHILD 
MIGHT EXPECT. THESE CHILDREN--OR MANY LIKE THEM--ONE DAY MIGHT 
HAVE A RED MISSION IN THEIR HOMELAND. 

GRADUALLY, THEY WERE TOLD THEY NEED NOT BELIEVE “ALL THAT SILLY 
STUFF ABOUT GOD," THAT THERE WAS ONLY ONE GOD AND HIS NAME WAS 
LENIN, HIS PROPHET STALINe ALL THE REST WAS LEGEND. 

ADULT REPATRIATES NEWLY ARRIVED IN THIS NORTHERN GREEK TOWN RECOUNT 
SUCH THINGS WITH FIERCE ANGER. 

MANY OF THE CHILDREN WERE CHOSEN FOR SPECIALIZED INDOCTRINATION. 
MANY OTHERS, PARTICULARLY AMONG THOSE WHO WERE DRIVEN ACROSS THE 
BORDERS WITH THEIR FAMILIES AT THE HEIGHT OF THE RED RETREAT, FELL HEIR 
TO HARSH TREATMENT INSTEAD. 

IN ALL, POSSIBLY 50,000 PERSONS EITHER WERE DRIVEN OR FLED 
VOLUNTARILY ACROSS THE BORDERS IN THE CIVIL WAR. OF THESE, ABOUT 
28,000 BY OFFICIAL GREEK ESTIMATE WERE CHILDREN. IN VIRTUALLY ALL 
“ASES, CHILDREN WERE SEPARATED FROM PARENTS AND PLACED IN SPECIAL 
SCHOOLS FOR TRAINING. 

ATHENA KORANIS, NOW 17, WAS ONE WHO DID NOT GET THE SPECIAL 
TREATMENTe SHE ARRIVED BACK IN HER NATIVE GREECE LAST DECEMBER AND 
STILL LIVES IN ONE OF TWO ABANDONED SCHOOLHOUSES IN KASTORIAs AS MANY 
AS 15 OR zO REPATRIATES MAY BE HOUSED IN A SINGLE SCHOOLROOM, SLEEP- 


ING IN SHIFTS.

BERLIN, APRIL 13 (AP) -COMMUNIST-SURROUNDED WEST BERLIN LOOKED 
TODAY FOR A NEW RED CRACKDOWN ON ITS TRAFFIC WITH THE SOVIET ZONE 
FOLLOWING EAST GERMAN CHARGES THAT THE WESTERN POWERS HAVE TURNED THE 
CITY INTO A SPY CENTER. 

THE EAST GERMAN CABINET LAST NIGHT ANNOUNCED THE ARREST OF 
521 "WESTERN AGENTS® AND THE LIQUIDATION OF "A CONSIDERABLE NUMBER OF 
ESPIONAGE AND TERROR GROUPS.” IT SAID THESE WERE BEING DIRECTED FROM 
ALLIED-OCCUPIED WEST BERLIN. 

THE RED REGIME SAID IT WOULD TAKE "ALL NECESSARY MEASURES" TO 
PROTECT THE EAST GERMAN STATE FROM WHAT IT CALLED THE WEST'S CRIMINAL 
ACTIVITIES BASED IN WEST BERLIN» 

WEST BERLIN CIRCLES ANTICIPATED THE COMMUNISTS WOULD PUT 
NEW RESTRICTIONS ON GERMANS MOVING BETWEEN THE ALLIED PART OF THE 
CITY AND THE EASTERN ZONE. MANY GERMANS LIVE IN ONE AREA AND WORK IN 
THE OTHER. OTHERS VISIT RELATIVES OR FRIENDS ACROSS THE BORDERS. 

ANY WEST BERLINER SEEKING TO ENTER THE EAST ZONE MUST OBTAIN A 
SPECIAL PERMIT FROM THE EAST GERMAN MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR. MOVEMENT

(ADVANCE) 6s SALONIKA, GREECE, APRIL 13 (AP)-"WHY DID THEY NOT SEND 
US BACK OUR CHILDREN WHEN WE ASKED FOR THEM-~-SIX OR SEVEN YEARS 
AGO?" THE GREEK OFFICIAL SAID. "WHY ARE THEY SO ANXIOUS NOW? 

"PERHAPS IT IS BECAUSE NOW MANY OF THE CHILDREN ARE GROWN UP AND 
READY. PERHAPS, FROM THE COMMUNIST WAY OF THINKING, THE TIME HAS 
ARRIVED. 

THE OFFICIAL WAS DISCUSSING WITH ME THE GRAVE PROBLEM OF GREEK 
REPATRIATES FROM COMMUNIST COUNTRIES, WHERE ANYWHERE FROM 35,000 TO 
50,000 GREEKS--THE MAJORITY YOUNG PEOPLE--HAVE BEEN KEPT SINCE THE 
CIUIL WARs THE COMMUNISTS NOT ONLY HAVE AGREED TO REPATRIATE SOME OF 
THEM NOW. THEY SEEM ANXIOUS TO SEND THEM IN LARGE NUMBERS. 

*TO DO THE WORK OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY IN GREECE, THEY WOULD RE- 
QUIRE ONLY A RELATIVE FEW," THIS OFFICIAL CONTINUED. "MOST OF THE 
REPATRIATED PEOPLE PROBABLY STILL ARE LOYAL GREEKS. BUT SURELY AMONG 
THE YOUNG PEOPLE NOW THERE MUST BE MANY WHO HAVE BEEN TURNED INTO 
CONVINCED COMMUNISTS." 

YOUNG BOYS, SNATCHED FROM THEIR PEASANT VILLAGES IN THE RUGGED 
MOUNTAIN AREAS OF NORTHERN GREECE, GIVEN SPECIAL TREATMENT IN A BIG

CITY UNDER CEASELESS INDOCTRINATION, ISOLATED FROM ALL OTHER INFLU- 
ENCES, MIGHT WELL HAVE BECOME CONVINCED IN SEVEN YEARS 

SURELY AMONG THEM ALSO MUST BE MANY YOUNG PEOPLE WHO WILL BE 
UNHAPPY BACK IN THEIR NATIVE VILLAGES, UNABLE TO FIND THE KIND OF 
WORK FOR WHICH THEY NOW HAVE BEEN TRAINED ABROAD, UNABLE TO HAVE ANY 
OF THE CONVENIENCES OF A MODERN CITY. 

THE 200 REPATRIATES IN KASTORIA, NEAR THE ALBANIAN BORDER, ARE 
HOUSED IN SQUALID SURROUNDINGS IN TwO ABANDONED SCHOOLKOUSES. 
UNANIMOUSLY THEY SEEM TO HATE THE COMMUNISTS AND ALL THEIR WORKS. 
THEY HOTLY DENY THERE HAVE BEEN ANY AGITATORS AMONG THEM, THAT ANY 
AMONG THEM EVER EXPRESSED THE WISH TO GO BACK TO THE COMMUNIST 
LANDS. BUT EVEN THESE PEOPLE DO NOT WANT TO WORK IN THE VILLAGES 
ANY MORE. THE MEN--AND THEY ARE NOT AMONG THE CHOSEN GROUPS 
SPECIALLY TRAINED ABROAD--WANT TO HEAD TO THE CITIES TO FIND WORK. 
MANY OF THEM DO NOT WANT TO GO BACK TO THE FARMS AT ALL. 

THESE PEOPLE REPRESENT THE FIRST TRICKLE, SOME 3,700 REPATRIATES. 
MANY OF THEM HAVE NOW BEEN RESETTLED IN VILLAGES. THEY ARE NOT 
THE PEOPLE WHO CAUSE THE GREEK AUTHORITIES THE GREATEST CONCERN. THE 
AUTHORITIES ARE WONDERING ABOUT THOSE TO COME--THE YOUNGSTERS GROWN TO 
MATURITY UNDER COMMUNIST TEACHING AND ISOLATION.

(ADVANCE) BANGKOK, THILAND, APRIL 13 (AP)-DOWN THE 18-MILE OLD 
ELEPHANT TRAIL TO BANGKOK'S ATRPORT GLIDED TWO SMART NEW CARS--A 
MERCEDES-BENZ AND A FORD THUNDERBIRD.

XING PHUMIPHON ADULDET THE MOST POWERFUL MAN IN THAILAND. OUT OF

TROUBLE SHOOTER FOR PRESIDENT EISENHOWER. ,

NISMe

GROUP TRIED TO OVERTHROW THE NEW REGIME. PIBULSONGGRAM, A LIEUTENANT

HE BECAME DEFENSE MINISTER, DEPUTY COMMANDER IN CHIEF OF THE

AN EARLY CONFERENCE BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND FRANCE IS se TOuny 
NECESSARY TO HELP RESOLVE THE INTERNAL CRISIS IN THIS COUNTRY. 

AN OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT PUBLICATION SUGGESTED THAT SUCH 
A MEETING SHOULD PRECEDE THE OPENING OF THE ASIAN-AFRICAN CONFERENCE 
IN BANDUNG APRIL 18. | 

ONCE THE INTERNAL SITUATION IS CLARIFIED, A SECOND MEETING IN JUNE 
yOULD INCLUDE BRITAIN FOR THE PURPOSE OF EXAMINING LARGER 
FAR EASTERN QUESTIONS. THESE WOULD INCLUDE INDOCHINESE ELECTIONS 
FORMOSA AND THE ADMISSION OF COMMUNIST CHINA TO THE UNITED NATIONS. 

THE GOVERNMENT'S VIEWS WERE GIVEN IN THE OFFICIAL ORGAN 
VIET NAM PRESS. IT SAID RECENT EVENTS IN VIET NAM PERMIT NO FURTHER 
DELAYS IN THE FRENCH-AMERICAN TALKS ORIGINALLY ANNOUNCED LATE IN 
FEBRUARY AFTER THE BANGKOK CONFERENCE OF THE MANILA PACT POWERS.

STRENGTH NOW IS AROUND 70,0003 FULL SUPPORT FOR PREMIER 
NCO DINH DIEM'S GOVERNMENT; THE ANTI-GOVERNMENT MOVEMENT OF THE 
BINH XUYEN AND THE POLITICAL - RELIGIOUS SECTS WHICH FRENCH ELEMENTS 
ARE SAID TO BE BACKING.

AND FRENCHMEN ARE MILES APART. THE FRENCH OFFICIALLY AND PRIVATELY 
ARE BITTERLY CRITICAL OF AMERICAN SUPPORT OF THE NATIONALIST, 
ANTI-COMMUNIST PREMIER IN HIS QUARREL WITH THE SECTS.

WASHINGTON, APRIL 14 (AP)=-THE STATE DEPARTMENT TONIGHT DESCRIBED 
AS “ENCOURAGING” THE REPORTED SOVIET ATTITUDE TOWARD A TREATY TO 
RESTORE AUSTRIA'S INDEPENDENCE. 

IN MOSCOW TODAY AUSTRIAN AMBASSADOR NORBERT BISCHOFF SAID HIS 
COUNTRY AND RUSSIA HAVE AGREED ON “PRACTICALLY ALL QUESTIONS" CON- 
CERNING THE -PACT. | 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID IN A STATEMENT THAT IT HOPES THE REPORTED 
AGREEMENT "MAY LEAD TO THE EARLY CONCLUSION OF A STATE TREATY FOR 


AUSTRIA." 

HOWEVER, THERE WAS NO COMMENT ON WHAT THE STATEMENT CALLED "THE 
SUBSTANCE OF THE QUESTIONS RAISED" IN DISCUSSIONS BETWEEN AUSTRIAN 
PREMIER JULIUS RAAB AND RUSSIAN OFFICIALS IN MOSCOW, 

THESE QUtoOTIONS ARE UNDERSTOOD TO INCLUDE SOVIET DEMANDS FOR 
GUARANTEES THAT AUSTRIA WILL NOT JOIN ANY ALLIANCES, PROVIDE ANY 
MILITARY BASES OR SUBMIT TO ANSCHLUS CUNION) WITH WEST GERMANY. 

THE DEPARTMENT SAID COMMENT ON THE SUBSTANCE WOULD AWAIT FURTHER 
STUDY OF DIPLOMATIC REPORTS AND CONSULTATION WITH BRITAIN AND FRANCE, 


WHICH PARTICIPATE WITH THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA IN THE OCCUPA- 
TION OF AUSTRIA.

BERLIN, APRIL 14 (AP)-THE COURT-MARTIAL OF AN AMERICAN SOLDIER 
WHO SPENT SIX YEARS IN SOVIET HANDS WAS HALTED AT THE MIDWAY POINT 
TODAY TO GIVE THE DEFENSE A CHANCE TO SEARCH FOR WITNESSES. 

AN ARMY COURT GRANTED PVT. WILLIAM T. MARCHUK, 39, OF NORRISTOWN, 
PAs, U TIL MAY 16 TO OBTAIN WITNESSES OR THEIR DEPOSITIONS. 

THE RULING WAS MADE ON A DEFENSE MOTION AFTER THE PROSECUTION 
CONCLUDED ITS CASE AGAINST THE SOLDIER CHARGED WITH DESERTING IN 
1949 AND GIVING INFORMATION TO THE RUSSIANS ABOUT HIS WEST BERLIN 
INTELLIGENCE UNIT» MARCHUK WAS RETURNED BY THE RUSSIANS LAST 
JANe 8 AFTER SIX YEARS IN VARIOUS LABOR CAMPS, INCLUDING VORKUTA. 

HE COULD GET A MAXIMUM OF 30 YEARS IF CONVICTED. 

THE PROSECUTION FILLED SEVEN STENOGRAPHER'S NOTEBOOKS WITH ITS 
CASE AGAINST THE SOLDIER, VIRTUALLY ALL OF IT TOP SECRET. | THE 

PRESS WAS BARRED FROM MOST OF THE THREE DAYS OF TESTIMONY GIVEN BY 
AMERICAN AND GERMAN WITNESSES. TO HAVE OPENED THE CASE TO THE PUBLIC 
WOULD HAVE EXPOSED THE METHODS USED BY COUNTER-INTELLIGENCE TO 
PENETRATE THE SOVIET EAST, OFFICERS SAID. 


IN THE ONLY PROTRACTED PUBLIC SESSION bs aaa TESTIMONY WAS 
D 


GIVEN TO SHOW THAT MARCHUK WAS PRO-COMMUNIST AND PRO-SOVIET IN THE 
PRISON CAMPS. A STATEMENT FROM JOHN H. NOBLE OF DETROIT, A CIVILIAN 
RELEASED WITH MARCHUK FROM VORKUTA, WAS READ TO THE COURT. NOBLE 
SAID MARCHUK HOBNOBBED WITH COMMUNIST INFORMERS, READ ONLY SOVIET 
LITERATURE, AND REFUSED TO CONSIDER HIMSELF A "REPRESENTATIVE OF 
AMERICA." ‘ 

IN CLOSED SESSION, THE COURT HEARD THE TESTIMONY OF A MAJOR AND A 
CAPTAIN, FORMERLY ON DUTY IN BERLIN, THAT MARCHUK REVEALED HIMSELF 

BE "PRO-RUSSIAN" JUST BEFORE HE DISAPPEARED FROM HIS UNIT. 

MARCHUK, SON OF _RUSSIAN-BORN PARENTS, HAS PLEADED INNOCENT TO 
BOTH DESERTION AND THE "AFFILIATION AND ASSOCIATION" WITH THE SOVIET 
MVD (SECRET POLICE). THE DEFENSE CONTENDED THE ARMY'S CASE WAS BASED 
ON HEARSAY, OBJECTED TO CLOSED COURT SESSIONS AND CAST DOUBT ON THE 
CREDIBILITY OF SOME OF THE WITNESSES. TO PROTECT THEIR IDENTITY, TH 
COURT-MARTIAL AREA WAS TIGHTLY GUARDED BY SPECIAL DETACHMENTS OF 


NTRY AND MILITARY POLICE.

WORLD BANK-IFC (450) 

WASHINGTON, APRIL 14 (AP)-THE 56-NATION WORLD BANK MOVED TODAY To 
SET UP THE PROPOSED 100-MILLION-DOLLAR INTERNATIONAL FINANCE CORP. (IFC) 

THE BANK ANNOUNCED THAT PRESIDENT EUGENE R» BLACK HAD SENT A PROPOSED 
CHARTER TO EACH MEMBER GOVERNMENT. HE DESCRIFED IT AS "A MOST 
SATISFACTORY FRAMEWORK" FOR ESTABLISHING THE LONG DISCUSSED INTERNAT- 
TONAL AGENCY TO ENCOURAGE THE INVESTMENT OF PRIVATE CAPITAL IN UNDER- 
DEVELOPED AREAS. 

MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ALL WORLD BANK COUNTRIES, ALL 56 OF WHICH ARE 
IN THE NON-COMMUNIST WORLD. 

SECRETARY OF THE TREASURY HUMPHREY ANNOUNCED LAST FALL THAT THE 
ADMINISTRATION WOULD BACK CREATION OF THE IFC AND WOULD PROPOSE To 
CONGRESS THAT THE UNITED STATES PUT IN THE LARGEST CAPITAL SUBSCRIPT- 
TON--$35,168,000. THE UNITED KINGDOM WITH $14,400,000 WOULD BE THE 
SECOND LARGEST INVESTOR, AND NATIONALIST CHINA WITH $6,646,000 WOULD 
BE THIRD. 

ALL CAPITAL QUOTAS IN THE IFC WERE BASED ON WORLD BANK SUBSCRIPTIONS. 
A BANK SPOKESMAN TOLD REPORTERS IT WOULD "PROBABLY BE DIFFICULT" FoR 
THE CHINESE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT TO FULFILL ITS QUOTA, SINCE ITS 
WORLD BANK SUBSCRIPTION WAS FIGURED AT A TIME WHEN CHIANG KAI-SHEK 
WAS STILL ON THE CHINA MAINLAND. 

THE SPOKESMAN SAID IT HAD BEEN INDICATED THAT FINLAND PROBABLY 
WOULD NOT JOIN, HAVING INFORMED THE WORLD BANK IT LACKS THE $421,000 
ALLOTTED AS ITS QUOTA. 

THE SPOKESMAN SAID A DRAFT OF THE CHARTER HAD BEEN CIRCULATED TO 
ALL MEMBER GOVERNMENTS AND REWRITTEN IN THE LIGHT OF THEIR COMMENTS. 
IT WAS APPROVED BY A MAJORITY OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTORS OF THE WORLD 
BANK, BUT THEIR MEMBER GOVERNMENTS MUST GIVE FINAL APPROVAL. 

THE IFC WOULD BE OPERATED BY THE WORLD BANK, BUT UNLIKE THE BANK IT 
WOULD PE ABLE TO MAKE INVESTMENT LOANS WITHOUT GUARANTEES FROM GOVERN- 
MENTS WHERE THE INVESTMENTS ARE MADE. SUCH AN ORGANIZATION HAS LONG 
BEEN URGED BY LATIN AMERICAN, ASIAN AND OTHER NATIONS WITH CHRONIC 
DOLLAR SHORTAGES FOR INTERNAL DEVELOPMENT. 

IFC, ACCORDING TO THE CHARTER CIRCULATED TODAY, WOULD: 

1, BE BASICALLY AIMED AT ENCOURAGING "THE GROWTH OF PRODUCTIVE 
PRIVATE ENTERPRISE IN ITS MEMBER COUNTRIES, PARTICULARLY IN THE LESS 
DEVELOPED AREAS OF THE WORLD." A SPOKESMAN FOR THE BANK SAID THIS 
WOULD INCLUDE LATIN AMERICA, AFRICA, ASIA, THE MIDDLE EAST AND PACIFIC

A CAMPAIGN FOR A NEW PLAN TO STOP RUSSIAN TANKS AT WEST GERNANY’S 
EASTERN BORDER RECEIVED NEW IMPETUS TODAY. THE INFLUENTIAL WEEKLY 
SOLDATEN ZEITUNG (SOLDIERS NEWSPAPER) THREW ITS WEIGHT BEHIND THE IDEA. 

THE WEST GERMAN PRESS IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY CRITICAL OF PRESENT 
NATO PLANS. THESE CALL FOR HIGHLY MOBILE WESTERN FORCES TO STEER 
RUSSIAN DIVISIONS INTO AREAS WHERE THEY CAN BE ATOM BOMBED OUT OF 
EXISTENCE. aS ERMAN CRITICS SAY, WOULD MAKE THICKLY POPULATED WEST 


GERMANY A BATTLEFIELD TWICE. 
FIRST, THEY SAY, THERE WOULD BE THE RUSSIAN ADVANCE. THEN WOULD 
COME THE COUNTERATTACK. 

TO PREVENT THIS, THEY URGE THAT THE NEW GERMAN FORCES MAN A 
STRONGLY FORTIFIED ANTITANK LINE ALONG THE IRON CURTAIN TO STOP ANY 
RUSSIAN ADVANCE INTO WEST GERMANY. THEY WANT WESTERN DIVISIONS KEPT 
IN RESERVE TO DRIVE THE RUSSIANS BACK INTO EAST GERMANY AFTER THE RED 
ASSAULT HAS BEEN CUT TO PIECES BY THE GERMAN DEFENDERS.

THE SQUTH. SOUTH KOREA CHARGED RED INSPECTORS IN THE SOUTH WERE

LATE LAST FEBRUARY, THE ALLIES CHARGED THE COMMUNISTS WITH 
ILLEGALLY INTRODUCING INTO NORTH KOREA AT LEAST 150 MIG JET FIGHTERS, 
THE CHARGE WAS SUPPORTED WITH AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHS TAKEN THE DAY 
THE ARMISTICE WAS SIGNED. THESE SHOWED THERE WAS NOT A SINGLE 

AIRFIELD IN NORTH KOREA CAPABLE OF HANDLING JETS. 

THE ALLIES SUBMITTED AERIAL AND GROUND RADAR TRACKINS TO PROVE 
THE PRESENCE OF RED JETS ON SIX FIELDS. THEY NOTED THE REDS THEM- 
SELVES ADMITTED THAT TWO MIGS SHOT DOWN WHEN THEY ATTACKED A U.S, 
PLANE OFF KOREA FEB. 5 HAD FLOWN OFF NRTH KOREAN FIELDS. 

AFTER MONTHS OF BRAGGING ABOUT FREEDOM TO INSPECT AND INVESTIGATE 
IN NORTH KOREA, THE CZECHS AND POLES WERE IN AN AWKWARD POSITION. 

THEY ARGUED FOR FIVE DAYS ON PROCEDURAL MATTERS. THEN THEY MADE 
A BIG SHOW OF AGREEING TO AN INSPECTION. BY THE TIME THE TRUCE TEAM 
REACHED THE AIRFIELDS IT COULD FIND NO EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL MIGS. 

THE UeNe COMMAND ANGRILY CHARGED THAT THE COMMUNISTS DELAYED 
THE TEAMS UNTIL THEY HAD TIME TO FLY THE MIGS INTO HIDING. 

A NEUTRAL OFFICER SAID THE INCIDENT WAS *MERELY ANOTHER IN THE 
SERIES OF COMMUNIST OBSTRUCTIONS THAT HAS MADE THE NEUTRAL NATIONS

SWEA CITY, IOWA, APRIL 15-CAP)-MRSs HAROLD FISCHER SR. 
AMERICAN AIRMAN IMPRISONED BY THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS, SAID 
SHE HAS RECEIVED A LETTER FROM U.N. SECRETARY-GENERAL DAG 

HA &gt; 

SHE SAID THAT HAMMARSKJOLD WROTE: 

*] WOULD LIKE YOU TO KNOW I AM CONTINUING EFFORTS” TOWARD THE 
RELEASE OF YOUR SON, CAPT. HAROLD FISCHER JR., AND *I WILL NOT RELAX 
AS LONG AS I SEE THE SLIGHTEST CHANCE OF suCcCEsS.° 

*I HAVE THE GREATEST SYMPATHY FOR YOUR WISH TO SEE YOUR SON. 
HOWEVER, I FEEL THE PRESENT TIME WOULD NOT BE APPROPRIATE FOR A 
YISITs THE SITUATION DEMANDS A GREAT DEAL OF PATIENCE AND A GOOD DEAL 
OF FORTITUDE BY SUCH AS YOURSELF WHOSE PRIVATION IS THE GREATEST." 

MRSe FISCHER ALSO SAID THAT IN A RECENT LETTER FROM HER SON 
CAPT. FISCHER WROTE THE AMERICAN PRISONERS HAD BEEN TOLD BY THEIR 
CUARDS THEY WOULD NOT BE RELEASED UNTIL THE UNITED STATES AGREES 
TO DEAL DIRECTLY WITH COMMUNIST CHINA. | 

MR. AND MRSe FISCHER SAID YESTERDAY THEY HAD RECEIVED A REPLY 
TO A LETTER THEY WROTE TO CHOU EN-LAI ACCEPTING A CHINESE INVITATION 
TO VISIT THEIR PRISONER OF WAR SON. 

THE FISCHERS SAID THEY PLAN TO RENEW THEIR REQUEST TO THE STATE 
DEPARTMENT FOR PASSPORTS SO THEY CAN FLY TO CHINA. 

PREVIOUSLY THE STATE DEPARTMENT HAD REJECTED REQUESTS OF ANY 
AKERICANS WHO WISHED TO ACCEPT THE CHINESE INVITATION TO VISIT CAPTIVE 
RELA . 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID YESTERDAY THERE WOULD BE NO COMMENT 
UNTIL THE FISCHERS’ REQUEST FOR A PASSPORT WAS RENEWED. 

MRS. FISCHER SAID SHE HOPES THE PROPOSED SENATE INVESTIGATIONS 
SUBCOMMITTEE INQUIRY INTO THE CASE OF THE IMPRISONED AMERICAN 
AIRMEN WOULD DO SOME GOOD. 

THE SUBCOMMITTEE PLANS TO START ITS INVESTIGATION MONDAY. 

CAPT. FISCHER, A DOUBLE JET ACE, HAS BEEN HELD BY THE CHINESE 
REDS SINCE HE waS SHOT DOWN NEAR THE YALU RIVER IN APRIL, 1952.

MORE OPENLY FRIENDLY TO THE WEST--THE PHILIPPINES, TURKEY, PAKISTAN, 
THAILAND, LIBERIA AND POSSIBLY JAPAN.

ESIDENT EISENHOWER TODAY 
ASES OF THE GOVERNMENT'S ANTI- 
COMMUNIST FOREIGN AID PROGRAM TO THE STATE AND DEFENSE DEPARTMENTS 
FROM THE FOREIGN OPERATIONS ADMINISTRATION (FOA). 

FOA, WHICH HAS BEEN HANDLING THE MULTI-BILLION-DOLLAR PROGRAM THE 
LAST TWO YEARS, IS SCHEDULED TO GO OUT OF BUSINESS JUNE 30, 

THE PRESIDENT ALREADY HAS NAMED THE AGENCY'S DIRECTOR, HAROLD 
E. STASSEN, TO A NEW JOB -- SPECIAL ASSISTANT TO THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE 
ON DISARMAMENT PROBLEMS. 

EISENHOWER SET FORTH HIS PLANS FOR THE SHIFT TO STATE AND DEFENSE 
IN A LETTER TO SECRETARY OF STATES DULLES WHICH WAS MADE PUBLIC AT THE 
PRESIDENT'S VACATION HEADQUARTERS HERE. THE PLANS WILL BE FORMALIZED 
IN AN EXECUTIVE ORDER TO BE ISSUED SHORTLY. 

THE TRANSFER OUTLINE WAS ANNOUNCED AS THE PRESIDENT MADE READY 
TO SEND CONGRESS A SPECIAL MESSAGE NEXT WEEK CALLING FOR ABOUT 
$3,530,000,000 (B) FOR WEAPONS AND ECONOMIC AID FOR SOME 40-opp 
COUNTRIES DURING THE FISCAL YEAR STARTING JULY 1. OF THE TOTAL 
AROUND $2,140,500,000 WILL GO TO STEP UP SUCH AID TO NON-COMMUNIST 
NATIONS IN ASIA.” 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT ALL ALONG HAS HAD POLICY SUPERVISION OF THE 
FOREIGN AID PROGRAM. UNDER THE NEW PLAN IT ALSO WILL HAVE SUPERVISING 
AUTHORITY OVER ACTUAL OPERATION OF THE ECONOMIC AID PHASE OF THE 

OPERATIONAL AUTHORITY OVER THE MILITARY AID ASPECTS WILL REMAIN 
WITH THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT, WHICH ALSO WILL TAKE OVER FROM FOA 
SERTAIN MILITARY-RELATED OPERATIONAL PHASES, SUCH AS PROVISIONS OF 
UNIFORMS AND SHOES.

BANDUNG, INDONESIA, MONDAY, APRIL 18 (AP)-IRAQ, THE FIRST ARAB 
NATION TO JOIN A PRO-WESTERN DEFENSE ALLIANCE, DENOUNCED COMMUNISM 
AT THE ASIAN-AFRICAN CONFERENCE TODAY AS A “NEW FORM OF COLONIALISM 
MUCH DEADLIER THAN THE OLD ONE.® ) 

THE DEFENSE OF ALLIANCES AGAINST COMMUNISM WAS MADE BY FADIL JAMALI, 
FORMER IRAQI PREMIER AND HEAD OF THE IRAQI CONFERENCE DELEGATION« 
IT WAS EXPECTED TO AROUSE THE ANGER OF RED CHINA'S PREMIER CHOU 
EN-LAI AND INDIA'S NEUTRALIST PRIME MINISTER NEHRU. 

SOME OBSERVERS THOUGHT IT MIGHT TURN THE 29-NATION CONFERENCE INTO 
ANOTHER EAST-WEST PROPAGANDA BATTLE« | 

IRAQ RECENTLY SIGNED A MILITARY PACT WITH TURKEY, A MEMBER OF THE 
NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION (NATO). BRITAIN LATER JOINED THE 
TRAQI“TURKISH ALLIANCE. IRAQ'S ACTION BROUGHT STRONG PROTESTS FROM 
EGYPT AND CAUSED A SPLIT IN THE ARAB WORLD. 

PAKISTAN AND EVENTUALLY IRAN ARE EXPECTED TO FOLLOW IN A STRING 
OF ALLIANCES ACROSS RUSSIA'S GATEWAY TO THE MIDDLE EAST. 

"WE BELIEVE SUCH MEASURES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR SELF PRESERVATION 
UNTIL SUCH TIME WHEN THE COMMUNISTS MAY CHANGE THEIR MINDS AND 
HEARTS AND AGREE TO A UNIVERSAL SYSTEM OF DISARMAMENT, INCLUDING 
THE PROHIBITION OF NUCLEAR WEAPONS,® JAMALI SAID IN A STATEMENT. 

JAMALI ISSUED HIS STATEMENT EARLY MONDAY AFTER IT WAS DECIDED 
TO DISPENSE WITH OPENING SPEECHES FROM DELEGATIONS AND CIRCULATE 
STATEMENTS OF POLICY. JAMALI SAID, HOWEVER, ANOTHER EFFORT MIGHT BE 
MADE TO DELIVER THE SPEECHES LATER. |

BY HAROLD MILKS 
(ADVANCE) BANDUNG, INDONESIA, APRIL 17 (AP)-THE BIG QUESTION 


$7).24- 1 CCD 


FACING RED CHINA'S PREMIER CHOU EN-LAI AT THE ASIAN-AFRICAN CONFERENCE 
IS THIS: “WHAT ARE YOU GOING TO DO ABOUT THE 12 MILLION OR MORE 


OVERSEAS CHINESE LIVING IN SOUTHEAST ASIA?* 
IT IS UNLIKELY THIS QUESTION WILL BE RAISED IN FORMAL CONFERENCE 


SESSIONS.» 

BUT SEVERAL COUNTRIES ARE VITALLY INTERESTED IN WHAT THE PEIPING 
GOVERNMENT IS GOING TO DO ABOUT MAKING CHINESE ABROAD CHOOSE BETWEEN 
THE NATIONALITY OF THEIR HOMELAND AND THAT OF THE COUNTRY IN WHICH 
THEY LIVE. 

THE QUESTION OF OVERSEAS CHINESE WITH DUAL CITIZENSHIP AND DUAL 
LOYALTIES ALWAYS HAS BEEN A VEXING PROBLEM IN COUNTRIES LIKE INDONESIA 
WHICH HAS MORE THAN THREE MILLION CHINESE; THAILAND AND BURMA WITH 
SMALLER CHINESE POPULATIONS. 

BURMA'S PREMIER U NU RAISED THIS QUESTION WITH CHOU NEARLY A 
YEAR AGO AFTER THE COMMUNIST PREMIER'S VISIT TO INDIA. AT THAT TIME 
BURMESE SOURCES SAID THE COMMUNIST CHINESE LEADER PROMISED HE WAS 
RETURNING HOME TO MAKE A FORMAL ANNOUNCEMENT THAT CHINESE LIVING ABROAD 
MUST CHOOSE ONE NATIONALITY -- EITHER THAT OF CHINESE OR THAT OF THE 
COUNTRY IN WHICH THEY ARE SETTLED. 

"BUT NOTHING HAS HAPPENED," SAID ONE BURMESE SOURCE HERE, “CHINESE 
MINORITIES IN OUR COUNTRIES STILL HAVE DUAL CITIZENSHIP AND STILL ARF 
RESPONSIBLE TO PEIPING, IF THAT NATION WISHES TO MAKE USE OF THEM." 

INDONESIAN AND THAI OFFICIALS HAVE EXPRESSED EQUALLY STRONG CONCERN 
OVER RED CHINA'S FAILURE TO CLEARLY MAKE PUBLIC ITS POLICY TOWARDS 
THE OVERSEAS CHINESE. 

WELL-INFORMED SOURCES HERE PREDICT NU WILL FIND TIME DURING THE 
CONFERENCE TO RAISE AGAIN THE QUESTION AND REMIND CHOU OF HIS PROMISE 


TO SETTLE IT. 
THEY PREDICTED INDIA'S PREMIER NEHRU WOULD SUPPORT NU 
TO WRING FROM THE CHINESE LEADER FRESH COMMITMENTS. w Recess 

IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT IT WAS NEHRU WHO FIRST BROUGHT SOUTHEAST 
ASIA'S CONCERN OVER DUAL NATIONALITY OF SUCH A LARGE SEGMENT OF ITS 
POPULATION TO CHOU"S_ ATTENTION, AND ADVISED HIM ITS SOLUTION WOULD 
ERASE CONSIDERABLE Dy WST AMONG HIS NEIGHBORS.

GOVERNMENT JOB AND STRIPPED HIM OF ALL HIS PARTY POSTS, 


THE PURGING OF THE 58-YEAR-OLD GOVERNMENT CHIEF HAD BEEN

HIM OF “RIGHT WING DEVIATIONISMe” HE HAD BEEN THE SPOKESMAN IN HUNGARY 
FOR THE “NEW LOOK" EMPHASIS ON CONSUMER GOODS PRODUCTION WHICH THE 
COMMUNIST COUNTRIES ABANDONED WITH THE DEMOTION OF GEORGI MALENKOYV 
FROM THE SOVIET PREMIERSHIP. |

SESSION CONVENING LATER THIS MORNING.

VIENNA, AUSTRIA, APRIL 17 CAP)-AUSTRIAN CHANCELLOR JULIUS RAAB SAID 


TODAY “THE AUSTRIAN GOVERNMENT AND PARLIAMENT WILL INVITE THE BIG FOUR 
POWERS TO TALKS ON THE AUSTRIAN STATE TREATY AS SOON AS POSSIBLE," 

RAAB SPOKE IN THE TOWN OF ST. POELTEN NEAR VIENNAe HE DID NOT 
DISCLOSE WHEN OR WHERE THE TALKS MIGHT BE HELD OR ON WHAT LEVEL. 

THE CHANCELLOR CAME HOME TRIUMPHANTLY FRIDAY FROM MOSCOW WITH SOVIET 
PROMISES TO END THE OCCUPATION NOT LATER THAN DEC. 31, 1955. A 
FINAL SETTLEMENT ALSO MUST HAVE THE APPROVAL OF THE UNITED STATES, 
BRITAIN AND FRANCE. 

AUSTRIAN INFORMANTS SAID YESTERDAY THE CHANCELLOR PLANS TO INVITE 
EITHER THE BIG FOUR CHIEFS OF STATE OR THEIR FOREIGN MINISTERS TO COME 
TO VIENNAs HE MAY ISSUE THE INVITATION IN A SPEECH TO THE JOINT SES- 
SION OF THE UPPER AND LOWER HOUSES OF THE AUSTRIAN PARLIAMENT ON 
APRIL 27, THE INFORMANTS SAID. 

THE OFFICIAL PRESS SERVICE OF RAAB'S AUSTRIAN PEOPLES PARTY SAID 
THE “FORM OF THE INVITATION® WOULD BE DECIDED ON BY THE AUSTRIAN 
PARLIAMENT, PROBABLY ON APRIL 28. 

SOCIALIST VICE CHANCELLOR ADOLF SCHAERF DISCLOSED IN A SPEECH ALSO 
DELIVERED IN ST. POELTEN THAT AUSTRIA HAS AGREED NOT TO SELL TO FOR- 
EIGNERS ANY OF THE INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISES IT WILL GET BACK FROM THE 
SOVIETS UNDER THE TREATY PROVISIONS. MOST OF THE INDUSTRIES WERE SO- 
CALLED “GERMAN ASSETS" SEIZED BY THE SOVIETS AFTER WORLD WAR IIe IN- 
CLUDED ARE OIL WELLS AND REFINERIES AND THE DANUBE STEAMSHIP COMPANY. 

RAAB, IN A RADIO REPORT TO THE NATION ON HIS MOSCOW MISSION, SAID 
THE TALKS WITH THE SOVIETS WERE "RELATIVELY EASYe® 

THE AUSTRIAN DELEGATION TOLD THE RUSSIAN LEADERS THEY ESPECIALLY 


WANTED THE RELEASE OF AUSTRIAN WAR PRISONERS AND INTERNEES STILL IN 
RUSSIA AND RETURN OF THE SOVIET ZONE INDUSTRIES, RAAB SAID. SUBSTAN- 
TIAL PROGRESS WAS MADE AFTER ONLY TWO HOURS OF TALKS, HE RELATED, AND 
THE SOVIETS FINALLY PROMISED CONCESSIONS THAT SHOULD MAKE IT POSSIBLE 
FOR AUSTRIA TO BE INDEPENDENT WITHIN A FEW MONTHS. THE AUSTRIANS, FOR 
THEIR PART, AGREED NOT TO JOIN ANY MILITARY ALLIANCES OR PERMIT 
MILITARY BASES ON AUSTRIAN SOIL. 

“WE THANK THE LORD FOR MAKING IT POSSIBLE THAT WE LIVED TO SEE THIs 
DAY," RAAB CONCLUDED. ®I AM VERY HAPPY, MY DEAR FELLOW CITIZENS, TO 
BE ABLE TO GIVE YOU THIS REPORT."

ISSUED BY SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES AFTER A 2-HOUR CONFERENCE WITH 
PRESIDENT EISENHOWER TODAY: 
"I GAVE THE PRESIDENT A REVIEW OF RECENT DEVELOPMENTS IN THE FIELD 


OF QUR FOREIGN RELATIONS. 
AS REGARDS REUROPE, I WAS ABLE TO REPORT A STEADY PROGRESS IN THE 
PROGRAM FOR BRINGING INTO FORCE THE TREATIES FOR GERMAN SOVEREIGNTY, 
GERMANY ENTRY INTO NATO AND THE CREATION OF WESTERN EUROPEAN UNION. 
I TOLD THE PRESIDENT THAT IT WAS HOPED TO HAVE A MEETING OF THE NATO 
MINISTERIAL COUNCIL EARLY IN MAY, ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT THE FEDERAL 
REPUBLIC OF GERMANY WOULD, BY THEN, BE ELIGIBLE TO ATTEND, AND THAT AT 
THAT TIME THE FOREIGN MINISTERS WOULD EXPECT TO DISCUSS AND, I HOPED, 
ADVANCE CONCRETE PLANS FOR NEW DISCUSSIONS WITH THE SOVIET UNION. 

"WE DISCUSSED THE DEVELOPMENTS REGARDING AUSTRIA, ALL THE FACTS ARE 
NOT YET KNOWN AND, UNTIL THEY ARE, NOTHING SHOULD BE TAKEN FOR 
GRANTED. BUT ON THE BASIS OF WHAT IS KNOWN, IT SEEMS THAT THE WESTERN

CHICAGO, APRIL 17-(AP)-A FORMER OFFICIAL OF THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMIS- 
TED TODAY HE HAS OBSERVED INSTANCES WHERE GOVERNMENTAL SECUR- 


SION ASSER 
ITY AND INFORMATION CONTROLS HAVE “HELPED KILL THE GROWTH" OF POTENTIAL- 


LY IMPORTANT INDUSTRIAL ACTIVITIES.» 
JeGe BECKERLEY, AEC DIRECTOR OF CLASSIFICATION FROM 1949 TO 1954, 


ADDED: 

"I SAW OTHER CASES WHERE SECURITY CONTROLS EXCLUDED JUST THOSE PER- 
SONNEL MOST LIKELY TO CONTRIBUTE KEY IDEAS, PERHAPS THE TECHNOLOGICAL 
BREAKTHROUGHS NEEDED TO CONVERT LABORATORY “RUBE GOLDBERGS" TO RELIABLE 
AND USEFUL INDUSTRIAL MACHINESs 

®AND IN MANY OF THESE INSTANCES I COULD FIND LITTLE EVIDENCE THAT THE 
SECURITY CONTROLS PROVIDED COMPENSATING GAINS IN THE NATIONAL 


STRENGTHKe"® 
HE WAS A CONTRIBUTING AUTHOR TO A SPECIAL ISSUE OF THE BULLETIN OF 


THE ATOMIC SCIENTISTS DEVOTED ENTIRELY TO AN ANALYSIS OF THE GOVERN- 
MENT'S SECURITY-LOYALTY POLICIES. 

ALL THE AUTHORS OF THE 15 ARTICLES SUGGESTED CHANGES IN THE LOYALTY- 
SECURITY PROGRAM BUT NONE PROPOSED THAT IT BE DISCARDED. 

EDWARD SHILS, PROFESSOR IN THE COMMITTEE ON SOCIAL THOUGHT AT THE UNI. 
VERSITY OF CHICAGO AND SPECIAL EDITOR OF THE ISSUE, SAID THE PROGRAM 
SHOULD BE "RETAINED, CONCENTRATED AND IMPROVED." HE ADDED: 

"IT SHOULD BE RETAINED BECAUSE THERE IS DANGER OF ESPIONAGE WHICH Is 
ACTIVE AND PERSISTENT. IT SHOULD BE CONCENTRATED AND IMPROVED BE- 
CAUSE, AT PRESENT, THE AMERICAN SECURITY SYSTEM FLINGS ITS NOT TOO 
WIDELY AND INDISCRIMINATELY, BECAUSE IT CONFUSES THE NEED FOR SECURITY 
WHICH IS READL, WITH HE NEED FOR PROTECTION FROM SUBVERSIVES, WHICH Is’ 
WHICH IS REAL, WITH HE NEED FOR PROTECTION FROM SUBVERSIVES, WHICH IS 
NEGLIBLE, AND BECAUSE IT MAKES DEMANDS FOR MAXIMUM LOYALTY WHICH ARE 
NEITHER NECESSARYFOR SECURITY NOR ADMISSIBLE TO THE IDEA OF FREEDOM.”

ANTHONY EDEN WAS REPORTED TODAY TO HAVE TOLD INDIA'’S PRIME MINISTER 
NEHRU THAT THE INDOCHINA TRUCE COMMISSIONS ARE NOT PROPERLY CARRYING 
OUT THEIR ROLES UNDER THE GENEVA AGREEMENTS+ | 

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES SAID EDEN CRITICIZED THE COMMISSIONS IN A 
LETTER HE WROTE AS CO-CHAIRMAN OF THE GENEVA CONFERENCE, WHICH ENDED 
THE INDOCHINA WARe THE LETTER WAS ADDRESSED TO NEHRU AS PRIME 
MINISTER OF THE COUNTRY WHICH HOLDS THE CHAIRMANSHIP OF THE TRUCE 
COMMISSIONS. 

THE INFORMANTS SAID EDEN'S LETTER STATED THAT THE TRUCE COM- 
MISSIONS" MAIN JOB WAS TO SUPERVISE THE TRUCE AND INVESTIGATE ALLEGED 
VIOLATIONS BUT THAT THE COMMISSIONS, UNDER INDIA, WERE MORE INTER- 
ESTED IN FINDING A PERMANENT SOLUTION OF THE INDOCHINA CRISIS. | 

THE LETTER IS SAID TO HAVE ANGERED NEHRU, WHO NORMALLY IS ON FRIEND~

THE STALIN AN HIERARCHY CONTINUED ITS RETURN TO THE HARD POLICY OF

P (OF MATYAS RAKOSI, TOUGH FIRST SECRETARY OF THE HUNGARIAN 
COMMUNIST PARTY AND THE REAL BOSS IN HUNGARYe IT PARALLELED THE 
EMERGENCE OF OPEN DOMINATION BY NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV, RUSSIA'S 


COMMUNIST PARTY CHIEF. 
NAGY, A RUSSIAN-TRAINED, OLDTIME COMMUNIST REVOLUTIONARY, REPLACED 


RAKOSI AS PREMIER IN JULY, 1953, FOUR MONTHS AFTER STALIN'S DEATH. 
RAKOSI STAYED ON AS THE NOs 1 MAN IN THE PARTY POLITBURO, WHILE 
NAGY BECAME THE FRONT MAN FOR THE REGIME AND ITS NEW EMPHASIS ON 
INCREASED PRODUCTION OF CONSUMER GOODS. 

RAKOSI, 63, HAS HAD A LONG, BRILLIANT AND OFTEN VIOLENT CAREER 
IN INTERNATIONAL COMMUNISM. HE WAS IN RUSSIA IN WORLD WAR II AND 
RETURNED HOME WITH ADVANCING SOVIET ARMIES. LONG CONSIDERED STALIN'S 
HATCHETMAN IN HUNGARY, HE HAS BEEN THE REAL POWER IN HIS COUNTRY SINCE 
i9 456 
IT WAS RAKOSI WHO, SHORTLY BEFORE MALENKOV LOSTHIS TOP JOB IN 
MOSCOW, ANNOUNCED AFTER A VISIT TO THE SOVIET CAPITAL THAT HUNGARY 
WOULD RETURN TO ITS STALIN-ERA EMPHASIS ON RODUCTION OF HEAVY 
INDUSTRY. 

THE OUSTER OF FARKAS CAME AS A SURPRISE TO MANY WESTERN OBSERVERS 
WHO HAD CONSIDERED HIM A LIKELY SUCCESSOR TO THE PREMIERSHIP. HE Hap 
PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED INVIENNA AS HUNGARY'S DEFENSE MINISTER 
BUT TODAY'S ANNOUNCEMENT DID NOT CONNECT HIM WITH ANY GOVERNMENT 
OST. 

NAGY'S ASSOCIATION WITH THE COMMUNISTS DATED BACK TO 1917 
WHEN HE FOUGHT IN RUSSIA AT THE OUTBREAK OF THE REVOLUTION. BETWEEN THE 
WARS HE WORKED HIS WAY UP IN HUNGARY'S COMMUNIST PARTY AND DURING WORLD 
WAR II HE RETURNED TO RUSSIA AS A HUNGARIAN LANGUAGE BROADCASTER. 

THE RED ARMY BROUGHT HIM BACK TO HUNGARY IN 1944 AND HE ENJOYED A 
RAPID RISE IN THE NEW RED REGIME. AFTER SERVING AS AGRICULTURE 
MINISTER, INTERIOR MINISTER AND PARLIAMENT SPEAKER, HE WAS NAMED ONE 


OF FIVE VICE PREMIERS UNDER RAKOSI.

WE ASIAN AND AFRICAN COUNTRIES NEED TO COOPERATE IN THE ECONOMIC AND 
CULTURAL FIELDS IN ORDER TO FACILITATE THE ELIMINATION OF ECONOMIC AND 
CULTURAL BACKWARDNESS DUE TO THE LONG PERIOD OF COLONIAL 
EXPLOITATION AND EXPRESSION. 

THIS COOPERATION SHOULD BE BASED ON EQUALITY AND MUTUAL BENEFIT 
WITH NO CONDITIONS FOR PRIVILEGE ATTACHED. TRADE RELATIONS AND ECONOMIC 
COOPERATION BETWEEN US SHOULD HAVE FOR ITS PURPOSE THE PROMOTION OF 
INDEPENDENT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN EACH COUNTRY AND NOT TO CONVERT 
ANY COUNTRY INTO A SOLE PRODUCER OF RAW MATERIALS AND MARKET FOR CON- 
SUMER GOODS. OUR CULTURAL EXCHANGE SHOULD HAVE RESPECT FOR DEVELOPMENT 
OF NATIONAL CULTURE OF EACH COUNTRY AND NOT IGNORE THE CHARACTERISTICS 
AND SPECIAL MERITS OF CULTURE OF ANY COUNTRY SO THAT WE MAY LEARN AND 
BENEFIT FROM EACH OTHER. 

TODAY WHEN THE PEOPLES OF ASIA AND AFRICA ARE INCREASINGLY TAKING 
THEIR DESTINY INTO THEIR OWN HANDS, EVEN THOUGH PRESENT ECONOMIC AND 
CULTURAL COOPERATION AMONG OURSELVES CANNOT YET BE OF VERY LARGE SCALE, 

IT CAN DEFINITELY BE SAID THAT THIS COOPERATION, BASED ON EQUALITY AND 
MUTUAL BENEFIT, WILL HAVE A GREAT FUTURE. WE ARE CONVINCED THAT 

WITH THE ADVANCEMENT OF INDUSTRIALIZATION OF OUR COUNTRIES AND THE RAISING 
OF OUR PEOPLES’ STANDARDS OF LIVING AND WITH THE ELIMINATION OF ARTI- 
FICIAL TRADE BARRIERS PLACED BETWEEN US FROM 4 gee LN TRADE INTERCOURSE 
AND ECONOMIC COOPERATION AMONG ASIAN AND AFRICAN COUNTRIES WILL BECOME 
EVER CLOSER AND CULTURAL INTERFLOW WILL BE EVER MORE FREQUENT. 

IN THE INTEREST OF DEFENDING WORLD PEACE, WE ASIAN AND 

AFRICAN COUNTRIES WHICH ARE MORE OR LESS UNDER SIMILAR CIRCUMSTANCES 
SHOULD BE FIRST TO COOPERATE WITH ONE ANOTHER IN A FRIENDLY MANNER AND 

PUT PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE INTO PRACTICE. DISCORD AND SEPARATION CREATED 
AMONG THE ASIAN AND AFRICAN COUNTRIES BY COLONIAL RULE IN THE PAST

BONN, GERMANY, APRIL 19 CAP) THE UNITED STATES PLANS TO DEPOSTT IN 
BONN TOMORROW THE TREATY TO RESTORE WEST GERMAN SOVEREIGNTY. 

WITH THIS ACTION, THE UNITED STATES WILL BECOME THE FIRST NATIO 
TO DEPOSIT THE TREATY TO FREE WEST GERMANY OF 10 YEARS OF ALLIED 
OCCUPATION. 

A WEST GERMAN OFFICIAL SAID TODAY THE UNITED STATES HAS NOTIFIED THE 
BONN GOVERNMENT THAT HIGH COMMISSIONER JAMES CONANT WILL DEPOSIT THE 
TREATY TOMORROW MORNING. 

A CEREMONY WILL BE HELD IN THE PRESENCE OF CHANCELLOR 
KONRAD ADENAUER AND OTHER HIGH AMERICAN AND WEST GERMAN OFFICIALS. 

THE CEREMONY WILL BE HELD AT THE PALAIS SCHAUMBURG, THE GERMAN 
WHITE HOUSE. 

THE SOVEREIGNTY TREATY WILL BECOME EFFECTIVE ONLY WHEN THE OTHER 
SIGNATORY NATIONS--BRITAIN, FRANCE, AND WEST GERMANY--FORMALLY 
DEPOSIT IT. ALL HAVE RATIFLED IT. 

BRITISH AND WEST GERMAN OFFICIALS SAID THESE THREE POWERS 
PLAN TO DEPOSIT THE TREATY TOGETHER AT A LATER DATE. 

THE TREATY TO ADMIT WEST GERMANY TO THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY 
ORGANIZATION (NATO) WILL BE DEPOSITED IN WASHINGTON. THE TREATY TO

IN THE FIGHT AGAINST PREMLER NGO.DINH DIEM’S AMERICAN-SUPPORTED 
GOVERNMENT. TERRORISTS MADE A HIT-AND-RUN ATTACK ON THE HOTEL 
MAJESTIC, SAIGON'S BIGGEST, WITH A MACHINEGUN AND HAND GRENADES. 
FRENCHMAN WAS WOUNDED. 

THE ATTACK ON THE SIX-STORY HOTEL WHERE MANY AMERICANS AND FRENCH~- 
MEN LIVE CAME SIX HOURS AFTER THE BINH XUYEN PRIVATE ARMY HAD SHELLED 
THE VIETNAMESE NATIONAL ARMY HEADQUARTERS TWO MILES AWAY. TEN 
NATIONALIST SOLDIERS AND TWO BINH XUYEN COMMANDOS WERE WOUNDED IN A 
50-MINUTE BATTLE. 

A SERIES OF OTHER CLASHES SHOOK THIS CAPITAL CITY OF TWO MILLION. 
ALL AMERICAN PERSONNEL WERE ORDERED OFF THE STREETS. FRENCH UNION 
TROOPS WERE ALERTED. 

THE ATTACK ON THE MAJESTIC, LOCATED IN THE CENTER OF THE FRENCH 
RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT, WAS MADE BY A TRUCKLOAD OF MEN, WHO RACED 
OFF AFTER FIRING THE MACHINEGUN AND HURLING TWO HAND GRENADES. THE 
FIRE WAS DIRECTED AT THE CROWDED SIDEWALK BAR WHERE 10 MEMBERS OF THE 
AMERICAN TRAINING MISSION WERE SIPPING DRINKS. 

AN UNOCCUPIED UsSe AIR FORCE CAR PARKED NEARBY WAS RIDDLED WITH 
BULLETS.s THE FIRST GRENADE DID NOT EXPLODE. THE SECOND DID, 
SERIOUSLY WOUNDING A FRENCHMANs 

NO ONE WAS IMMEDIATELY ABLE TO IDENTIFY THE MEN IN THE TRUCK. 

BUT THE FRENCH HAVE SAID FOR SEVERAL DAYS THAT THE BINH XUYEN, A % 
POLITICAL ORGANIZATION OF FORMER RIVER PIRATES BITTERLY opposer 
PREMIER DIEM, INTENDED TO BEGIN TERRORISTIC ACTS AGAINST AMERI :

THE BOMBARDMENT OF THE NATIONAL ARMY HEADQUARTERS IN THE HEART

AT LEAST 26 PERSONS WERE KILLED AND 112 WOUNDED IN THAT CLASH. 

IN ONE SKIRMISH YESTERDAY, THE ARMY CHARGED THE BINH XUYEN WITH 
KIDNAPING A NATIONAL SOLDIER AND LATER FIRING ON TWO ARMY VEHICLES, 
KILLING THE DRIVER OF ONE. 

THE BULK OF THE FIRING ON THE ARMY HEADQUARTERS TODAY CAME FROM 
A PRINT SHOP ABOUT 100 YARDS AWAY. WHEN NATIONALIST ARMORED CARS 
WHEELED IN FRONT OF IT, THE OCCUPANTS HAD VANISHED. BUT HALF AN 
HOUR AFTER THIS FIRING HAD SUBSIDED, A NATIONAL ARMY JEEP WAS RIDDLED 
BY FIRE FROM THE SAME BUILDING AND TWO OF ITS SOLDIER OCCUPANTS WERE 
WOUNDED. |

APRIL 19 (AP)-THE WESTERN ALLIES AND RUSSIA TOOK LONG 
STEPS TODAY TOWARD A MEETING ON AUSTRIAN INDEPENDENCE AND PERHAPS LATER 
SESSIONS ON THE GERMAN AND COLD WAR ISSUES. 

A SOVIET CALL FOR AN EARLY CONFERENCE TO SIGN AN AUSTRIAN INDEPENDENCE 
TREATY BROUGHT SPEEDY AMERICAN ASSURANCE THAT IT IS RECEIVING "PROMPT 
AND SYMPATHETIC CONSIDERATION.” 

A STATE DEPARTMENT STATEMENT ADDED THAT THE UNITED STATES AND ITS 
BRITISH AND FRENCH PARTNERS ALREADY ARE "EXPLORING THE MOST EXPEDITIOUS 
METHODS® OF RESTORING AUSTRIA TO "HER RIGHTFUL STATUS OF SOVEREIGN 
INDEPENDENCE,® 

THE RUSSIANS HAVE SUGGESTED, IN A NOTE HANDED UsSe AMBASSADOR CHARLES 
E, BOHLEN AT MOSCOW, THAT THE BIG THREE OCCUPYING POWERS MEET "IN THE 
NEAREST. FUTURE™ WITH AUSTRIAN OFFICIALS AT VIENNA TO SEE ABOUT SIGNING 

THE OFFICIAL AMERICAN STATEMENT RECALLED THAT THE UNITED STATES 
BRITAIN AND FRANCE HAD "CONSISTENTLY PRESSED® RUSSIA FOR AN AUSTRIAN 
‘SETTLEMENT FOR NINE YEARS. IT SAID THE UNITED STATES "IS GLAD TO LEARN® 
MOF SOVIET WILLINGNESS TO GO ALONG NOW. 

BOTH THE SOVIET SUGGESTION AND THE AMERICAN REACTION REFERRED TO LAST 
eSe

RUSSIA WILLING, THE FOUR AMBASSADORS COULD HANDLE TREATY TALKS WITH | 

AUSTRIAN OFFICLALS AT VIENNA.

AND NAVY HAVE VARIED IN REQUIREMENTS FOR COMPLETING LOYALTY PROCEDURES.

TO TAKE THE STANDARD OATH OF LOYALTY AND ALLEGIANCE TO THE UNITED

THIRD NIGHT LEAD ASIAN-AFRICAN (€280)) ¥ OO 
BY ROBERT HEWETT 

BANDUNG, INDONESIA, THURSDAY, APRIL 21 (AP)-THE ASIAN-AFRICAN 
POLITICAL COMMITTEE TODAY APPROVED AN ARABAESOLUTION ON THE PALESTINE 
PROBLEM. IT CALLED FOR PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT OF THE DISPUTE WITH ISRAEL 
ON THE BASIS OF UNITED NATIONS RESOLUTIONS. 

RED CHINA'S PREMIER CHOU EN-LAI, WHO HAS BEEN WOOING THE ANTI- 
COMMUNIST ARAB STATES AT THE 25-NATION CONFERENCE, ASSISTED IN DRAFT- 
ING THE RESOLUTION WHICH THE COMMITTEE ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY. 

ARAB LEADERS CONSIDERED THE RESOLUTION A VICTORY FOR THEIR CAUSE, 
SINCE ISRAEL IN THE PAST HAS REFUSED TO COMPLY WITH U.Ne RESOLU- 
TIONS WHICH WOULD REQUIRE THE JEWISH STATE TO REPATRIATE ARAB 
REFUGEES AND PROVIDE COMPENSATION FOR LAND LOST IN ISRAELe SHE ALSO 
HAS REFUSED TO INTERNATIONALIZE JERUSALEM AND CEDE DISPUTED 
TERRITORY TO THE ARABS ON A PARTITION PLANe 

APPROVAL BY THE FULL CONFERENCE IN A PLENARY SESSION LATER WAS A 
CERTAINTY SINCE THE POLITICAL COMMITTEE IS COMPOSED OF THE 29 CHIEFS 
OF DELEGATIONS. 

THE RESOLUTION READS? 

“IN VIEW OF THE EXISTING TENSION IN THE MIDDLE EAST CAUSED BY THE 
SITUATION IN PALESTINE AND OF THE DANGER OF THAT TENSION TO WORLD PEACE, 
THE ASIAN~5;~-!488-, $9,1343,33 $33)-RES ITS SUPPORT OF THE RIGHTS OF THE 
ARAB PEOPLE IN PALESTINE AND CALLS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE UNITED 
NATIONS RESOLUTIONS ON PALESTINE AND THE ACHIEVEMENT OF PEACEFUL 
SETTLEMENTS OF THE PALESTINE QUESTION.® 

— WAS NOT INVITED TO THE CONFERENCE BY THE SPONSORING COLOMBO 
POWERS. 

ALTHOUGH THE RESOLUTION DOES NOT MENTION ISRAEL BY NAME, ITS 
SUPPORT OF THE PALESTINIAN ARABS AND ITS CALL FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF 
UeNe RESOLUTIONS OPPOSED BY ISRAEL WERE INTERPRETED BY ARAB LEADERS 
AS CONDEMNATION OF THE JEWISH STATE. 

THE RESOLUTION AS ADOPTED WAS THAT PRESENTED BY AFGHANISTAN'S 
DELEGATION BUT WITH THE ADDITION BY THE SUB-COMMITTEE OF THE LAST 
PHRASE CALLING FOR A PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT. 

INDIA AND BURMA ADDED THIS TO THE PROPOSAL. INDIA'S PRIME MINISTER 
NEHRU SAID THE BACKGROUND OF NAZI PERSECUTION OF THE JEWS SHOULD BE 
CONSIDERED AND THAT FURTHER NEGOTIATION BETWEEN ARABS AND JEWS 
SHOULD NOT BE RULED OUT, 

CHOU, WHO EXPRESSED HIS SYMPATHY FOR ARAB REFUGEES IN YESTERDAY 
DEBATE. DROPPED HIS FIRST OBJECTION TO MENTION OF THE UeNe RESOLUT 
NEW PROBLEMS APPEARED ON THE CONFERENCE HORIZON, TESTING THE 

ABILITY OF ITS LEADERS TO STEER A HARMONIOUS COURSE. BUT THE 
JAPANESE DELEGATION PROMISED ONE RAY OF HOPE. JAPAN, THE FIRST 
VICTIM OF ATOMIC WARFARE, HAD A PLAN FOR WORLD PEACE. ITS DELEGATE 
SAID IT WOULD BE PRESENTED TO THE POLITICAL COMMITTEE ON FRIDAY. 

THE TEXT OF THIS PLAN WAS KEPT SECRET. 

“IT IS A WORLD PLAN-- A GLOBAL SCHEME FOR PEACE,” SAID ONE 
DELEGATE. 

JAPAN'S CHIEF DELEGATE TATSUNOSUKE TAKASAKI WAS RESTING IN 
PREPARATION FOR PRESENTING THE PROGRAM.

BANDUNG, INDONESIA, APRIL 20 (AP)-RED CHINA'S~GHOU EN-LAI IS 
WOOING THE MOSLEMS AT’ THE ASIAN-AFRICAN CONFERENCE BY PROPOSING TO 
BUILD A MOSQUE IN PEIPING. 

HIS PROPOSAL TO BUILD A MOSLEM RELIGIOUS SHRINE IN THE CHINESE 
CAPITAL WAS DISCUSSED WITH EGYPT'S PRIME MINISTER GAMAL ABDEL NASSER 
WHEN THE TWO MET IN RANGOON, INFORMED SOURCES SAID. CHOU ASKED 
NASSER'S HELP IN SENDING A DELEGATION OF MIDDLE EAST MULLAHS WHEN THE 
MOSOUE WAS COMPLETED, 

EGYPT AND MOST MIDDLE EAST COUNTRIES HAVE NOT GRANTED DIPLOMATIC 
RECOGNITION TO RED CHINA, BUT CHOU IS WORKING HARD TO WIN NEW MOSLEM 
FRIENDS AT THE CONFERENCE. 

ONE SOURCE CLOSE TO THE EGYPTIAN DELEGATION SAID THERE IS A GOOD 
CHANCE EGYPT'S MILITARY REGIME WOULD RECOGNIZE RED CHINA AFTER 
NASSER'S RETURN TO CAIRO. 

ANOTHER INDUCEMENT CHOU IS HOLDING OUT IS THE PROSPECT OF BIGGER 
CHINESE PURCHASES OF EGYPTIAN COTTON. COTTON IS THE BACKBONE OF 
EGYPT'S ECONOMY. LOWER PRICES RESULTING FROM Us Se PRODUCTION HAVE 
HIT EGYPT HARD. EGYPT ALREADY EXPORTS SOME COTTON TO RED CHINA, BUT 
CHOU IS REPORTED TO HAVE TOLD NASSER HE IS READY TO INCREASE HIS 
COTTON PURCHASES SUBSTANTIALLY IF A TRADE DEAL IS WORKED OUT.

THE THEORY IS EXPOUNDED IN *®THE LIMITS OF SOVIET POWER,” A BEST
